BathymetryReconstructionConfig.description:
Opt-in carving of the real lake bed from bathymetry into the grid.

When set, the loaded ``lake_bathymetry`` raster is resampled onto the lake
cells and (by default) reconciled to the abacus by area-weighted quantile
mapping, then carved into the mesh ``top``/``botm`` so the LAK vertical
exchange happens at the real bed and the groundwater flow lines follow the
real basin instead of a flat reservoir. The raster must be declared in the
data layer (``[data.lake_bathymetry]``); a lake without that data and with
reconstruction enabled raises at build time.

reconcile_to_abacus.description: Re-map the regridded bed so the cell area-vs-elevation distribution matches the abacus (the abacus is the storage source of truth). When False, the raw regridded bathymetry is carved as-is.
reconcile_to_abacus.title: Reconcile To Abacus

dynamic_area.description: Active-littoral (marnage) representation. When True the lake-bed cells stay ACTIVE with the carved bathymetric bed as their cell top and one VERTICAL LAK connection each; MODFLOW 6 then toggles recharge/ET per cell (IWETLAKE) so a cell exchanges with the lake when submerged and recharges as land when the shoreline recedes below its bed. When False the footprint is deactivated (fixed-area reservoir, the classic inactive-footprint carve).
dynamic_area.title: Dynamic Area

exposed_band_runoff.description: Shed the overland runoff of the exposed lakebed band directly to the lake, sized per timestep from the simulated stage via the MODFLOW 6 BMI API (runoff_rate * exposed_area). Requires dynamic_area and forces the in-process API runner (serial only). When False the catchment runoff already covers the footprint area in a lumped, stage-static way.
exposed_band_runoff.title: Exposed Band Runoff

bank_seepage.description: Also emit HORIZONTAL (bank) LAK connections on the active-littoral footprint, in addition to the VERTICAL (bed) ones, so the lake exchanges with the aquifer through both the bed AND the banks (the physical case). Sealed at the cutoff wall (dam) when one is declared. Only applies with dynamic_area = true; a fixed-area lake always emits both. Set False to keep the bed-only marnage representation (the bedleak then absorbs the bank contribution).
bank_seepage.title: Bank Seepage

min_thickness.description: Minimum layer thickness, in metres, held by EVERY layer when re-grading a lake column around the carved bed, so no degenerate (near-zero) cell breaks the solver. The bed is clamped into the band the column can hold at that floor, i.e. [base + n_active * min_thickness, top - n_occupied * min_thickness]; a column too thin for it raises at build time. Raising this value moves the carved bed away from the bathymetry (the build logs the shift).
min_thickness.title: Min Thickness

min_pixels.description: Minimum bathymetry pixels whose centre must fall inside a cell for the zonal mean to be used; below it a bilinear sample at the cell centroid is taken instead. A count of pixels.
min_pixels.title: Min Pixels

BathymetryReconstructionConfig.title: BathymetryReconstructionConfig

BedRegularizationConfig.description:
Least-change regularization of the channel bed in the model top.

A DEM read along its own channel rises downstream at many pixels: a deck, a
hedge, a resampling artifact. A drain or a stream cell on such a rise cannot
drain into the next one. On the pixels of the generated channel tree only,
the regularization fits the bed closest to the ground in least squares that
never rises downstream (the isotonic regression on a tree of Pardalos and
Xue, 1999), raising and lowering alike, then gives every pooled flat a
minimum drop centered on its level. The pixels a crossing notch lowered are
gaps: interpolated along the channel, never pulling the fit. A declared
weir or dam cuts the tree, so its drop is kept, and a declared lake is left
out with its surface.

It writes a regularized copy of the ground, and the model top and the SFR
bed read it, so drains and stream reaches see one bed. The routing DEM, the
channel tree, the catchment and the mesh never read that copy.

enabled.description: Regularise the channel bed of the model top: the least-change fit of the ground that never rises downstream along the channel tree, with the crossing notches as gaps and the declared weirs and dams as drops. Needs [geographic.river_network] enabled.
enabled.title: Enabled

min_slope.description: Minimum drop of the fitted bed per metre along the channel (m/m), given to the flats the fit pools. The SFR default slope.
min_slope.title: Min Slope

BedRegularizationConfig.title: BedRegularizationConfig

CalibNetworkBoundWeights.description:
How the two maps of a network output share one calibrated value.

A root search closes one root per map and returns the weighted geometric
mean, ``log K = permanent * log K*_permanent + complete * log K*_complete``.
A minimiser has no root to combine and minimizes
``permanent * |J_permanent| + complete * |J_complete|`` instead, which tends
to land on one of the two roots rather than between them.

permanent.description: Weight of the permanent map, scored against the minimal mask.
permanent.title: Permanent

complete.description: Weight of the complete map, scored against the maximal mask.
complete.title: Complete

CalibNetworkExtent.description:
The transient two-bound mode of a network output.

Declared, the output stops reading one state. For every complete calendar
year of the run, the maximal simulated mask holds the cells flowing for at
least ``flowing_at_least``, and the minimal one the cells flowing at every
timestep but for at most ``dry_at_most``. A cell enters the mask scored when
it meets the rule in at least ``year_quorum`` of the scored years. Each bound
is scored once by the distance criterion: the maximal mask against the
complete map, the minimal mask against the permanent map when one is declared.
Both durations are converted to whole timesteps with the run's step, so the
same file means the same on a daily and a monthly run.

flowing_at_least.description: How long a cell has to flow in a year to enter the maximal mask, with its unit: '30 d', '1 month'. Converted by the run's timestep, rounded up to whole timesteps and never below one. Left out, one timestep, whatever the step. At most the shortest complete year, checked on the run.
flowing_at_least.title: Flowing At Least

dry_at_most.description: How long a cell may be dry in a year and stay in the minimal mask, with its unit: '1 d', '1 month'. Converted by the run's timestep and rounded down to whole timesteps, possibly none: '1 d' is one dry timestep on a daily run, none on a monthly one. Left out, one timestep, whatever the step. The year's timesteps minus these have to stay at least the flowing timesteps of the maximal rule, checked on the run, so the minimal mask sits inside the maximal one.
dry_at_most.title: Dry At Most

year_quorum.description: Share of the scored years in which a cell has to meet a bound's rule to enter it: ceil(year_quorum * n_years) years. Warned under three scored years, where one half is a union of two.
year_quorum.title: Year Quorum

visible_flow.description: Routed discharge a cell of the downstream closure has to carry to flow: a discharge with its unit ('1 L/s') or a share of the outlet discharge at the same timestep ('1%'). '0 L/s' is the geometric definition. Never scaled with the cell size. It exists in this transient mode only: an output read in one state scores the closure alone. No value is agreed: Zanetti et al. (2024) threshold a simulated discharge at 10 L/s, field zero-flow thresholds of 1 to 3 L/s are in use.
visible_flow.title: Visible Flow

CalibNetworkExtent.title: CalibNetworkExtent

CalibNetworkMap.description: What is observed: the mapped network, its role in the cost and how it is drawn.

complete.description: The complete map, every mapped reach: a vector file, read only from here, or 'data.hydrography', the network the hydrography data family loaded (a local file or an osm / bdtopage / euhydro download), clipped to the delineated catchment.
complete.title: Complete

permanent.description: The permanent map, the reaches that flow all year, which the complete map contains: a vector file, read as it is and never filtered by attribute, or 'data.hydrography', the permanent reaches the hydrography data family wrote beside its network. A source that does not say which reaches flow all year gives none. The complete map scored is the union of the two, and the share of this map outside the complete one is published.
permanent.title: Permanent

calibrate_on.description: The role of each map, required when both are declared and refused otherwise. 'permanent' or 'complete' names the map in the cost. In one state, the other map is scored at the same state as a validation outside the cost, and 'permanent' is how Abherve et al. (2025) calibrate. With 'model.extent', the named map has all the weight. A table {permanent = 0.5, complete = 0.5} shares the value between both bounds, and only 'model.extent' scores two bounds.
calibrate_on.title: Calibrate On

drawn_by.description: How the map is drawn on the mesh cells. 'crossing' keeps the cell holding each point where a line crosses the segment joining two edge-sharing cell centres. On a structured grid it reproduces WhiteboxTools VectorLinesToRaster, the paper's tool, and draws the map one cell wide like the simulated network, so a model that matches the map scores J = 0. 'touch' keeps every cell the line touches, corners included, and replays a session made before 2026-09; it thickens every diagonal step of the map and departs from the paper. 'heads' keeps only the free ends of the map whose largest drained area within 'heads.radius' does not exceed that of the other end of their reach, lands each on a nearby cell and draws the rest down the criterion's own descent: the field ditches and rectified reaches below a head stop counting as model error, and the drawn map reaches the outlet. Keep 'crossing' for a map that is not a tree: canals, braids, polders, karst.
drawn_by.title: Drawn By

heads.description: Where a head may land, read only under drawn_by = 'heads' and refused under another rule. Left out under 'heads', the defaults of its keys.

clip_to_catchment.description: Cut the map to the delineated catchment before drawing it, with the shape the hydrography data family clips what it loads to, so a file and 'data.hydrography' draw the same map from the same data. Under 'heads' an end the cut made is no stream head. false reads a file whole and takes every free end as a candidate head.
clip_to_catchment.title: Clip To Catchment

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

position_accuracy.description: Positional accuracy of the map. It enters the automatic validity length only, so it is refused beside a 'verdict.validity_length' written as a length: the cell size h there is max(h_obs, this), because a map is not placed better when the mesh is refined. r_optim stays D_optim / h_obs, the paper's Eq. 3. Unset is the literal reading of the paper.
position_accuracy.title: Position Accuracy

CalibNetworkModel.description: How the model draws its own stream network.

seepage_threshold.description: A cell releasing less than this fraction of the mean basin recharge, taken over its own area, is not a seepage face. Zero reproduces the purely geometric criterion of the paper. Frozen over the whole search: a threshold moving with the trial would cost the criterion its monotonicity.
seepage_threshold.title: Seepage Threshold

neighbours.description: The graph the descent walks. 'D8' descends over shared nodes, the eight neighbours of a quad mesh, and is the paper: its distances are traced by WhiteboxTools on a D8 pointer, and the delineation that produced the catchment uses one too. 'D4' descends over shared edges only and departs from the paper. It is not a second-decimal choice: on a synthetic valley whose talweg runs along the grid diagonal, the most accumulated cell collects 100 per cent of the domain over shared nodes and 6.6 per cent over shared edges. On a mesh whose faces are not all quadrilaterals no cell has a diagonal and the descent walks shared edges either way; on a Voronoi mesh the two graphs are the same one.
neighbours.title: Neighbours

weighting.description: Average one cell one vote (the paper) or weighted by cell area. Both values are always reported; use 'area' on a mesh refined along the streams, where cell density is highest exactly where distances are smallest.
weighting.title: Weighting

value_docs.area: Every cell counts in proportion to its area.
value_docs.cell: Every cell counts once in the average, as in the paper.

extent.description: The transient two-bound mode. Unset, the output reads one state, the method of the papers. Set, it reads every timestep of a transient run and scores the maximal simulated mask against the complete map and, when 'map.permanent' is declared, the minimal mask against the permanent map. Refused on a run with a single period or no complete calendar year.

CalibNetworkModel.title: CalibNetworkModel

CalibNetworkVerdict.description: When the result of a network output is qualified or refused.

max_catchment_mismatch.description: Largest gap allowed between the scored catchment and the delineated one, as a share of the delineated area: 'catchment_mismatch', the area of their symmetric difference over the area of the outline the mesh followed. It depends on the geometry alone, so it is read once, before the first solve, and a gap above it refuses the search. A large gap means an outlet on another branch, or a mesh too coarse for the catchment. false never refuses, and the gap is still published on every trial. A synthetic domain has no delineated catchment and is never refused.
max_catchment_mismatch.title: Max Catchment Mismatch

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

validity_length.description: Validity bound of Eq. 4, a length: the calibration is valid when D_optim <= this. 'auto' is 2 h, the paper's two cells, where h is h_obs, the cell size on the mapped network, raised to 'map.position_accuracy' if that is declared. A length such as '150 m' is used as it is. The bound qualifies the result and never penalises the cost.
validity_length.title: Validity Length

on_invalid.description: What a violation of Eq. 4 does: D_optim above 'validity_length'. The bound is read once, on the trial the search returns, as the paper reads it at the optimum, and on each bound in the cost of the two-bound mode; every trial still records 'r_optim', 'r_optim_valid' and 'validity_length_m'. 'warn' logs it and returns the value, because a calibration is asked for a number. 'error' raises after the session is saved, so a staged calibration freezes nothing and runs no phase that depends on this one.
on_invalid.title: On Invalid

alpha_warning_threshold.description: Below this value of 'alpha_obs_closure_catchment' the run warns that its distances carry a top-versus-map disagreement on top of the hydrogeology. alpha is the share of the downstream closure of the mapped network the network itself covers, measured on the MODEL TOP and on the catchment. It changes nothing that is computed: the criterion is scored the same way above and below it.
alpha_warning_threshold.title: Alpha Warning Threshold

clipping_warning_share.description: Share of the mapped stream cells lying outside the delineated catchment above which the whole-mesh alpha is reported as unreadable. Those reaches trace through the buffer, where no cell is required to descend into the network, so they inflate the closure without adding to the numerator. Reported together with clipping_warning_gap, never alone.
clipping_warning_share.title: Clipping Warning Share

clipping_warning_gap.description: Minimum absolute gap between the whole-mesh and the catchment alpha for the clipping report to fire. A linework spilling out of the catchment over ground that routes the same way leaves the two ratios equal, and reporting it there would be noise on every ordinary project.
clipping_warning_gap.title: Clipping Warning Gap

CalibObjectiveBlockDecl.description:
Weighted metric block used by a composite objective.

A block consumes one or more named outputs, applies one metric, and
contributes ``weight`` to the final minimization cost. Blocks make mixed
objectives explicit, for example combining heads, discharge, and transport
signals in one calibration session.

name.description: Unique block identifier used in logs and persistence.
name.title: Name

metric.description: Metric that scores this block against its observations.
metric.title: Metric

value_docs.distance_gap: Balances the simulated stream network against the mapped one; zero marks the crossing.
value_docs.distance_mean: Mean spatial offset between simulated and mapped streams; a diagnostic, not a substitute for distance_gap.
value_docs.kge: Kling-Gupta efficiency, 2009 form (bias as the ratio of sums, variability as the ratio of standard deviations); separates correlation, variability and bias when NSE alone is ambiguous.
value_docs.mae: Mean absolute error, in the observed unit; less sensitive to outliers than RMSE.
value_docs.nse: Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency against the observed mean; the standard choice for a level or discharge series.
value_docs.nse_delta: NSE on the increments of the series rather than its level; a level is an integral and can hide flux errors that compensate, which only its increments show.
value_docs.nse_log: NSE on log-transformed series; weights low flows as heavily as peaks, good for recessions.
value_docs.nse_seasonal: NSE against the seasonal cycle rather than the overall mean; asks whether the model beats climatology.
value_docs.reservoir: Half nse_seasonal plus half nse_delta, built for an impounded level: a plain NSE there is beaten by the seasonal cycle, and the increments are what carry the flux errors.
value_docs.rmse: Root-mean-square error, in the observed unit; penalizes large misfits most.

weight.description: Weight of this block in the sum of the block costs. Only the ratios between weights matter.
weight.title: Weight

uses_outputs.description: Outputs (by name) consumed by this block. An error metric (rmse, mae) or a network distance may read several, pooled into one cost. A metric that rises with the fit (nse, kge and the other efficiencies) reads exactly one: write one block per output, each with its weight, so the costs average per station.
uses_outputs.title: Uses Outputs

normalize_cost.description: When True, divide the block cost by a reference scale, so it adds to other blocks as a pure number and a share means a share. On a residual metric (rmse, mae) the scale is the standard deviation of the observations, their mean absolute value if that is zero. On a network distance (distance_gap, distance_mean) it is the output's validity_length, 2 h_obs under 'auto': a gap of one validity length costs 1, as much as an NSE of 0 on nse_log. Refused on an efficiency score, already a pure number.
normalize_cost.title: Normalize Cost

cost_transform.description: Transform applied to the cost of this block before weighting. Note that cost_transform='log' takes the logarithm of the cost, which is not the same thing as metric='nse_log', an NSE computed on log-transformed series.
cost_transform.title: Cost Transform

value_docs.identity: Uses the block cost as computed, with no transform.
value_docs.inverse: Takes -1 / (cost + epsilon), sharpening the gradient near a cost of zero.
value_docs.log: Takes log10 of the cost plus a small epsilon, compressing large costs before weighting.

CalibObjectiveBlockDecl.title: CalibObjectiveBlockDecl

CalibOutputNetwork.description:
The mapped stream network as a calibration target.

The criterion compares a simulated stream network to a mapped one. For
every cell of the simulated network the descent to the mapped network is
measured, and reciprocally. The output produces the pair ``(D_so, D_os)``;
the metric on top of it is ``distance_gap``, their signed difference in
absolute value, whose zero is the balance between an excess of simulated
stream and a missing one.

It can drive any parameter that moves where the water table meets the
surface. What it identifies depends on what moves: with the homogeneous
conductivity alone, at fixed geometry and recharge, it identifies ``K/R``,
the ratio of Abherve et al. (2023), and not ``K`` itself.

There is no ``observed_values`` here and there cannot be: the criterion
balances two simulated quantities against each other, so nothing in it is
fitted to a record. The mapped network enters as a geometry, not as a
series. Three tables hold the rest: ``map`` is what is observed, ``model``
how the model draws its network and ``verdict`` when the result holds.

variable.description: Per-cell observable read from the solver, in m3/s, positive when the aquifer feeds the surface.
variable.title: Variable

support.description: Discriminator: compare a simulated stream network to a mapped one.
support.title: Support

map.description: What is observed: the mapped network, its role and how it is drawn.

verdict.description: When the result of this output is qualified or refused.

time.description: Which single state the release flux is read at: 'last' (default), 'first', or an ISO date such as '2002-10-15', which reads the state of the period that holds it, (start, end]. That state is dated at its period's end, which is the date a window is compared with. A steady phase runs one period over its window, so every date of that window reads its one state and one output serves both regimes. 'all' and a list of dates are refused: a network output reads one state.
time.title: Time

Observable extracted at a planar ``(x, y)`` point.

Use this variant for piezometric heads sampled at a single coordinate.
Provide either ``x`` and ``y`` or a GeoJSON ``geometry`` block.

The record is aligned on the simulated timestamps, so a weighted block scores dated observations rather than a vector typed into the file. The data family follows 'variable': discharge from hydrometry, head from piezometry, stage from lake_levels. Mutually exclusive with 'observed_values'. The station is located by its own record and not by coordinates written beside it, so this output and the single-metric route read the same cell and their costs are comparable; a station the project cannot locate is refused by name rather than scored on another quantity.

Accepts a bare number (metres) or a pint string like '150 m'; it is a maximum displacement, measured from the gauge coordinate to the cell centres. The drained area is the one the solver routes on the mesh, along the descent D of the build. Only for 'variable' = 'discharge'. With 'observes', a discharge station is then located by the coordinate of its record, which it otherwise is not, and snapped from there. CalibParameterDecl.description:
User declaration for one calibrated parameter.

The declaration is read from ``[calibration.parameters.<name>]``, and the
section name is the quantity: it is resolved against the catalog the
project exposes, so a file states the range and nothing else. Writing
``path`` is the way out for whatever the catalog does not reach, and it
wins without a lookup.

Use ``mode="replace"`` for direct parameter values and ``mode="scale"``
for multiplicative factors applied to an existing config value.

bounds.description: [low, high] physical bounds, in 'units' when the file writes it, else in the unit the target declares. Falls back to what the field annotates when the file omits it, which most fields deliberately leave unset because a range belongs to the site.
bounds.title: Bounds

search_space.description: Space the search walks the parameter in. 'log' for strictly-positive quantities spanning orders of magnitude. Unset, the target's own field decides: a hydraulic conductivity declares 'log' where it is defined, so a file states this only to depart from it.
search_space.title: Search Space

value_docs.log: Searches the logarithm of the value: for a positive quantity that spans orders of magnitude.
value_docs.logit: Searches log(x / (1 - x)): for a share strictly between 0 and 1. Both bounds must lie inside (0, 1).

sampling.description: Distribution, between the bounds, that starting points, random draws and Bayesian samplers take values from.
sampling.title: Sampling

value_docs.log_uniform: Every decade between the bounds is equally likely.
value_docs.normal: A normal law centred between the bounds, with a standard deviation of a sixth of their span, cut at the bounds.
value_docs.uniform: Every value between the bounds is equally likely.

path.description: Dotted TOML path of the value to move, such as 'flow.param.K.field.value'. Optional, and the way out rather than the way in: when omitted, the section name is resolved against the project catalogue ('hmp config targets' lists it). Write one to reach a value the catalogue does not carry, or to settle a name two targets answer to. A path written here wins without a lookup. When the catalogue carries it, the parameter inherits the field's space and draw like a named one; when it does not, nothing is inherited and the sample is written as it is drawn.
path.title: Path

target.description: Readable alias for 'path'. Setting both is refused.
target.title: Target

mode.description: 'replace' writes the sampled value as-is; 'scale' multiplies the base TOML value at the target path by the sample.
mode.title: Mode

units.description: Unit the bounds are written in, such as 'm/s'. For a parameter the catalogue resolves, bounds in another unit of the same quantity are converted when the file loads into the unit the target is read in, and the search draws, writes and reports its samples in that unit ('hmp config targets' lists it). A unit of another quantity is refused. Unset, the unit of the target applies. With mode = 'scale' the bounds are factors without a unit, and writing one is refused. For a path outside the catalogue it is the unit the bounds are checked against the physical range in.
units.title: Units

CalibParameterDecl.title: CalibParameterDecl

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

CalibPhaseDecl.description:
One stage of a calibration that runs in several.

A phase selects, by name, from the parameters, outputs and objective blocks
the calibration already declares: nothing is redeclared, so the two stages
of a method cannot drift apart in a single file. What a phase carries of
its own is its search: a method, a budget, and which parameters it is
allowed to move.

``freeze_on_success`` means this phase passes the values it found to the
phases after it. A later phase holds them fixed, unless it lists the
parameter: it then moves it again, starting from the passed value when its
method accepts a start point. It reads "pass on if the search settled",
never "pass on if the result is good": the engine met its own rule or
solved every point of its plan, or an engine with no rule of its own (a
random search) spent its budget, which the phase then says. A validity
indicator qualifies a result, and a phase that returns a coarse agreement
still returns a number.
The state of that indicator travels to the later phases and into the
report, so a value calibrated on top of a doubtful one carries the mention
all the way out.

name.description: Phase identifier, unique in the calibration and used in the session directory and in the report.
name.title: Name

description.description: What this phase calibrates and against what, in one sentence.
description.title: Description

method.description: Optimization method for this phase only. Unset, the phase runs the method [calibration] writes; failing that it follows from what the phase scores: 'bisection' when the phase moves one parameter in log space and every one of its blocks is signed (distance_gap), since the answer is then a zero to find; 'scipy_nelder_mead' otherwise, a cost to minimise. hmp calibrate --list-phases prints the method and where it comes from. Write it to depart from that choice, and whenever method_options are given and [calibration] writes no method. Built-ins: 'grid' (regular sweep, sized by method_options.points_per_dim), 'lhs' (stratified Latin hypercube, sized by method_options.n_samples), 'random_search', 'bisection' (root of a signed criterion on one parameter, the stream-network stage), 'optuna' (TPE), 'cma_es', 'scipy_de', 'scipy_nelder_mead' and 'gp_mapping'. An unknown name is refused when the optimizer is built, with the list installed here.
method.title: Method

anyOf.description: Positive integer.

max_trials.description: Maximum number of evaluations for this phase. Unset, the phase takes the max_trials of [calibration]. 'auto' lets an engine that counts its evaluations size it: the bisection budgets its worst case, the grid and the Latin hypercube their design, and each refuses before the first solve a number below its nominal count (see [calibration].max_trials). Any other engine gets 100 from 'auto', and no extension when it spends them before its stopping rule.
max_trials.title: Max Trials

anyOf.description: Positive floating-point value.

precision.description: How precisely the search has to pin a parameter before it stops, as a relative precision on the parameter itself: 0.01 asks for one per cent, 0.1 for ten. On a parameter searched in log space that is a ratio, which is how a conductivity is known in the first place, and it holds wherever the value sits; on any other search space there is no scale on the value to be relative to before the search has one, so it reads as a fraction of the declared interval. Each engine's own stopping option is written from it, so the same number survives a change of engine, and the engine's own option stays available for reproducing a published call verbatim. Unset, the phase takes the precision of [calibration] when its engine stops on one and the phase writes no stopping option of its own, else the engine's default applies. Written here, an engine that stops on its budget rather than on a precision refuses it rather than ignore it.
precision.title: Precision

batch_size.description: Suggestions drawn per ask, at least ``parallel``. Unset, the phase takes the ``batch_size`` of ``[calibration]``.
batch_size.title: Batch Size

parallel.description: Trials of this phase solved side by side, each in its own folder. Unset, the phase takes the ``parallel`` of ``[calibration]``, which also reaches the phases a protocol writes.
parallel.title: Parallel

parameters.description: Names of the calibration parameters this phase may move. Every other parameter keeps the value it entered the phase with.
parameters.title: Parameters

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

bounds.description: [low, high] physical bounds this phase searches a parameter between, as {parameter = [low, high]}, in the unit the parameter declares. Only parameters the phase moves, and every interval has to lie inside the bounds of [calibration.parameters.<name>] (or the range the field annotates when the section writes none): a phase narrows a search, it never widens it. A parameter left out keeps the bounds of the section. hmp calibrate --list-phases prints them.
bounds.title: Bounds

outputs.description: Names of the calibration outputs this phase scores on. Empty means every declared output.
outputs.title: Outputs

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

objective_blocks.description: Objective blocks this phase evaluates. Empty means every declared block. A list names them and keeps their declared weight. A table gives each named block the phase's own share instead, {block = share}, normalised to sum to one like a block's weight already is; every key must be a declared block, and every share must be positive.
objective_blocks.title: Objective Blocks

variable.description: Name of the simulated variable, or of a [calibration.outputs] entry, that objective scores when this phase uses no objective block. Unset, the variable of [calibration] applies.
variable.title: Variable

objective.description: Metric scoring this phase's single simulated series, when the phase does not use objective blocks. Same vocabulary as a block's 'metric'.
objective.title: Objective

value_docs.distance_gap: Balances the simulated stream network against the mapped one; zero marks the crossing.
value_docs.distance_mean: Mean spatial offset between simulated and mapped streams; a diagnostic, not a substitute for distance_gap.
value_docs.kge: Kling-Gupta efficiency, 2009 form (bias as the ratio of sums, variability as the ratio of standard deviations); separates correlation, variability and bias when NSE alone is ambiguous.
value_docs.mae: Mean absolute error, in the observed unit; less sensitive to outliers than RMSE.
value_docs.nse: Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency against the observed mean; the standard choice for a level or discharge series.
value_docs.nse_delta: NSE on the increments of the series rather than its level; a level is an integral and can hide flux errors that compensate, which only its increments show.
value_docs.nse_log: NSE on log-transformed series; weights low flows as heavily as peaks, good for recessions.
value_docs.nse_seasonal: NSE against the seasonal cycle rather than the overall mean; asks whether the model beats climatology.
value_docs.reservoir: Half nse_seasonal plus half nse_delta, built for an impounded level: a plain NSE there is beaten by the seasonal cycle, and the increments are what carry the flux errors.
value_docs.rmse: Root-mean-square error, in the observed unit; penalizes large misfits most.

method_options.description: Options of this phase's method, named as that method names them: sweep_points for 'bisection', points_per_dim for 'grid', sampler for 'optuna'. They belong to one method, so a phase that gives them writes method beside them, or runs the method [calibration] writes. Unset, the phase takes the method_options of [calibration] when it runs the method that section writes, and none otherwise; an empty table states that it takes none. A key the method does not take is refused when the file loads. hmp config check names the phase.
method_options.title: Method Options

regime.description: Flow regime this phase runs, a property of the model and not of the search. 'steady' is one period over steady_window, by default the extent of [simulation.time]. 'transient' is the project's own time grid. Unset, the phase runs the model as the project and its overrides declare it.
regime.title: Regime

value_docs.steady: One period over steady_window, so the recharge over it averages to its mean. A steady solve carries no storage.
value_docs.transient: The project's time grid, with only the regime restated.

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

steady_window.description: Dates the steady period spans, as {start, end}, when regime = 'steady'. Unset takes the whole [simulation.time] window.
steady_window.title: Steady Window

overrides.description: Configuration values this phase runs with, as dotted paths into the project configuration. A phase that gives regime may not write here a path regime writes: that would say the same thing twice.
overrides.title: Overrides

window.description: Dates bounding the samples this phase scores on, replacing [calibration].window. start = the first date scored leaves a spin-up out of every block alike. A network output read in one state is dated at the stamp of that state, which has to lie inside the window.

depends_on.description: Name of the phase that must run first. The values it passes on enter this one fixed, except those this phase lists and moves again. When that phase freezes its values and its search stops on its budget before a rule of its own, this phase is refused rather than run on the values of the file.
depends_on.title: Depends On

freeze_on_success.description: Pass the values this phase found to the phases after it. A later phase holds them fixed, unless it lists the parameter: it then moves it again, starting from the passed value when its method accepts a start point. When two phases pass on the same parameter, the later one wins. Success means the search met its own rule or solved every point of its plan, not that its validity indicator is good. A search with no rule of its own (random_search, cma_es) that spends its budget also passes on its best trial, and the phase says it froze the best of a budget-only search. One with a rule that its budget stops first passes nothing on.
freeze_on_success.title: Freeze On Success

uncertainty.description: How wide this phase says its answer is, with the keys of [calibration.uncertainty]. A key written here wins for this phase; a key left out takes the section's value, then the default that follows what the phase scores: one mesh cell for a phase scored only by network distances, five per cent of the best cost otherwise. hmp calibrate --list-phases prints the width each phase reads and where it comes from.

CalibPhaseDecl.title: CalibPhaseDecl

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

CalibPhaseUncertaintyDecl.description:
How wide one phase says its answer is, key by key over ``[calibration.uncertainty]``.

Every key is optional and has the meaning it has in the section. A key
written here wins for this phase. A key left out takes the section's value,
then the default that follows what the phase scores. ``restarts`` and
``perturbation`` belong to a method: a phase that names another method than
the section does not inherit them.

method.description: How this phase's interval is obtained: 'cost_profile', 'multistart' or 'linearized', read as in [calibration.uncertainty] method.
method.title: Method

value_docs.cost_profile: Reads the range of sampled values whose cost stayed within cost_margin of the best, off the trace of the search. No extra model run.
value_docs.linearized: Linearizes the model about the optimum: one extra run per parameter gives a first-order covariance, and with it which parameters trade off.
value_docs.multistart: Repeats the whole search restarts times from different starting points and reports the spread of the optima. It can see a second basin.

restarts.description: How many times method='multistart' repeats this phase's search.
restarts.title: Restarts

anyOf.description: Positive floating-point value.

perturbation.description: Relative step of method='linearized' for this phase, as a fraction of each calibrated value.
perturbation.title: Perturbation

cost_margin.description: Width of this phase's interval, with its unit: '5%' is a share of the best cost, '75 m' a length, for a phase scored only by network distances. Unset here and in [calibration.uncertainty], one mesh cell for a phase scored only by network distances, five per cent of the best cost otherwise.
cost_margin.title: Cost Margin

CalibPhaseUncertaintyDecl.title: CalibPhaseUncertaintyDecl

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

CalibUncertaintyDecl.description:
How wide the search says its own answer is.

The calibrated value never moves: this block only decides what is reported
beside it. ``cost_profile`` reads the interval off the trials the search
already ran, so it costs no extra model run and rests on no error model. It
says what the search could not tell apart, which is a statement about the
trace and not a posterior.

method.description: How the interval around each calibrated value is obtained. 'cost_profile' reads the range of sampled values whose cost stayed within 'cost_margin' of the best, off the trace the search already produced, and costs no extra model run. 'multistart' runs the whole search 'restarts' times from 'restarts' different starting points and reports the spread of the optima it reaches, which is the only one of the two that can see a second basin; it costs that many times the runs. The calibrated value never moves either way: with 'multistart' it is the best of the restarts.
method.title: Method

value_docs.cost_profile: Reads the range of sampled values whose cost stayed within cost_margin of the best, off the trace of the search. No extra model run.
value_docs.linearized: Linearizes the model about the optimum: one extra run per parameter gives a first-order covariance, and with it which parameters trade off.
value_docs.multistart: Repeats the whole search restarts times from different starting points and reports the spread of the optima. It can see a second basin.

restarts.description: How many times the search is repeated by method='multistart'. Required by it and refused by any other method, because a number of restarts that nothing restarts is a statement about a run that did not happen. Each one is a full search: eight restarts of a hundred-evaluation phase is eight hundred model runs.
restarts.title: Restarts

anyOf.description: Positive floating-point value.

perturbation.description: Relative step the derivatives of method='linearized' are taken with, as a fraction of each calibrated value: 0.01 moves it by one per cent. Required by it and refused by any other method. Too small and the difference is solver noise; too large and it is no longer a derivative. One per cent is the usual starting point, and the honest check is to move it and see whether the reported width moves with it. 'linearized' costs one model run per parameter, reads derivatives around the answer instead of searching again, and is the only declared method that also reports which parameters trade off against which. It is first-order: exact where the model is linear about the optimum, approximate in proportion to the curvature, and not a posterior.
perturbation.title: Perturbation

cost_margin.description: Width of the interval, written with its unit. '5%' is a share of the best cost, the usual choice for an efficiency score. A criterion solved at zero, such as the stream-network gap, has no fraction of itself to take: write a length, '25 m', which is only read by a search scored only by network distances (distance_gap, distance_mean). A bare number is refused. Unset, it follows what the search scores: one mesh cell, in metres, for a search scored only by network distances, because a stream cannot move by less than a cell; 5%, five per cent of the best cost, otherwise. The cell is the median distance between the centres of neighbouring cells, measured by the network criterion on the mesh it scores. A phase may write its own, which wins. hmp config check refuses a share on a search scored only by network distances.
cost_margin.title: Cost Margin

CalibUncertaintyDecl.title: CalibUncertaintyDecl

Dates bounding the samples a metric is computed on.

A window in dates rather than in sample counts: it says the same thing
whatever the output frequency.

start.description: First date scored, ISO 8601. Unset means from the first sample.
start.title: Start

end.description: Last date scored, ISO 8601. Unset means up to the last sample.
end.title: End

CalibrationConfig.description:
Top-level ``[calibration]`` section.

The config selects the optimizer, iteration budget, candidate persistence
policy, parameter declarations, observable outputs, and objective blocks.
It is the user-facing schema used by CLI calibration and
``Project.calibrate``. This section and the shape of ``CalibrationReport``
are experimental until the rework of the calibration is published.

When no explicit objective block is declared, HydroModPy can synthesize one
from ``objective`` and ``variable`` if the matching output exists.

protocol.description: Published calibration method this file runs, named instead of retyped. A protocol writes the stages, their criteria and the model regimes they need, so the file states only what belongs to the site. Write the name alone, or a table carrying it plus the names this file uses for the parameters and outputs the method moves. Registered: 'matching_hydrographic_network' (Abherve et al., 2023, doi:10.5194/hess-27-3221-2023). A file that declares its own phases or objective blocks cannot also name a protocol.

method.description: Optimization method. Unset, it follows from what the calibration scores: 'bisection' when it moves one parameter in log space and every one of its blocks is signed (distance_gap), since the answer is then a zero to find; 'scipy_nelder_mead' otherwise, a cost to minimise. Write it to depart from that choice, and whenever method_options are given. A phase of [[calibration.phases]] names its own. Built-ins: 'grid' (regular sweep, sized by method_options.points_per_dim), 'lhs' (stratified Latin hypercube, sized by method_options.n_samples), 'random_search', 'bisection' (root of a signed criterion on one parameter, the stream-network stage), 'optuna' (TPE), 'cma_es', 'scipy_de', 'scipy_nelder_mead' and 'gp_mapping'. An unknown name is refused when the optimizer is built, with the list installed here. Optuna is installed by default; install the calibration extra for cma_es and Optuna's cmaes sampler.
method.title: Method

evaluator.description: What turns one parameter sample into a cost. Unset runs the HydroModPy pipeline, which is what every calibrated number in this repository was produced with. A string and not an enumeration: the values that resolve depend on what is installed beside HydroModPy, which is how a surrogate or a foreign model is named without a patch. This build also ships 'analytic_bowl', which runs no model and scores a closed-form surface whose minimum is the midpoint of each parameter's interval: it rehearses a whole search -- space, optimizer, stopping rule, report -- in milliseconds, against an answer known in advance.
evaluator.title: Evaluator

forward_model.description: What produces the simulated observables when the evaluator is the one that scores a model with the criteria of this file ('scored_forward_model'). The model answers the outputs declared under [calibration.outputs] and the objective blocks weigh them, so changing a metric or a weight is a change to this document and never a patch to the model. A string and not an enumeration: what resolves depends on what is installed beside HydroModPy, through the 'hydromodpy.calibration.forward_model' entry-point group. Unset runs 'linear_reservoir', the closed-form reservoir this build ships, which is how a set of criteria is rehearsed before a model is installed. Read by no other evaluator.
forward_model.title: Forward Model

anyOf.description: Positive integer.

max_trials.description: Maximum number of evaluations of the search. It is the only bound on how long a search runs: no method option counts evaluations of its own. 'auto' lets an engine that counts its evaluations before the first solve size its own budget. Three do. The grid and the Latin hypercube count their design, one evaluation per point, and refuse a smaller number before the first solve, since a sweep cut short is not its design. The bisection counts with d the declared interval in decades, t = log10(1 + rel_tol), S the sweep points (counted as 2 for sweep_points 0), s = d / (S - 1) and E = bracket_expand, a root inside the bounds costs S + ceil(log2(s / t)) and one found after e expansions S + 2e + ceil(log2(1 / t)); 'auto' budgets the largest, 23 on [1e-7, 1e-3] m/s with seven points and one per cent (15 inside the bounds). A number below the nominal count is refused before the first solve, one below the worst case is announced, and a budget that still runs out gets exactly the halvings left, once. Any other engine gets 100 from 'auto' and no extension: a search that spends its budget before its own stopping rule is reported as not converged, and a re-run with a larger max_trials replays the trials already solved from the cache.

anyOf.description: Positive floating-point value.

precision.description: How precisely the search has to pin a parameter before it stops, as a relative precision on the parameter itself: 0.01 asks for one per cent, 0.1 for ten. On a parameter searched in log space that is a ratio, which is how a conductivity is known in the first place, and it holds wherever the value sits; on any other search space there is no scale on the value to be relative to before the search has one, so it reads as a fraction of the declared interval. Each engine's own stopping option is written from it, so the same number survives a change of engine, and the engine's own option stays available for reproducing a published call verbatim. Unset, the engine's default applies. An engine that stops on its budget rather than on a precision refuses this rather than ignore it.
precision.title: Precision

batch_size.description: Number of suggestions drawn per ask, at least ``parallel``.
batch_size.title: Batch Size

parallel.description: Trials solved side by side, each in its own folder, for every phase that sets none of its own. A grid or a random search evaluates its points together; a root search cuts its bracket into parallel + 1 parts; a simplex evaluates the candidates of one step together and keeps the sequential answer, so a width above 4 buys it nothing, and CMA-ES and differential evolution stop at their population. A width above 1 gives each worker process its own copy of the model (about 0.5 GiB, 3 s to start); 1 solves the trials one after the other in this process.

reject_water_budget_above.description: Percent water-balance discrepancy of the whole model past which a trial is rejected instead of scored. The figure is the one the solver prints for the volume budget of the entire model, not the budget of a single package such as the lake package, which divides by small flows and reads higher. A rejected trial is marked failed, so it is neither ranked nor promoted: part of the water it routed came from nowhere and its cost is not comparable to a run that closed. Default 1.0 (one per cent). Raise it for a transient model whose lake or routed network legitimately sits higher. A TOML file has no null: to switch the gate off write a value no run reaches, such as 1000, or pass None from Python. The worst time step of the run decides, not the last.

CappedBreachConfig.description:
Limits of the ``capped_breach`` DEM conditioning, in meters.

Read only when ``[geographic] dem_correc_type = "capped_breach"``. Least-cost
breaching digs a path through the barrier that closes a depression. These two
limits bound that digging, and whatever they refuse is filled instead. Both
are given in meters but the tool counts along the cells of a path (a sum of
lowerings, a number of cells), so a given value does not mean the same thing
at every grid resolution: see each field.

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

max_depth.description: Largest cumulative lowering, in metres, of one breach path (the 'max_cost' of Whitebox): the lowering summed over the cells of the path, not the depth of one cell. With short paths the realised maximum lowering of a cell stays close to it. On a finer grid a thick embankment spreads the cost over more cells, so it is filled instead of dug: the same value does not give the same landscape at every resolution. A depression whose cheapest breach costs more is filled. Paths overlap, so the lowering of a cell can exceed it (0.56 m for a value of 0.5 m, on a 75 m grid). The realised depth is measured after the call, logged, and warned about when it exceeds this value. Accepts inline units (e.g. 0.5, '0.5 m').
max_depth.title: Max Depth

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

max_distance.description: Longest breach path, in metres. Translated to the DEM grid as ceil(max_distance / cell size) cells, at least one, and counted in cells along the path: a diagonal step counts one cell, so a diagonal breach can be up to 1.41 times longer than max_distance. A depression with no way out within this length is filled. Accepts inline units (e.g. 200, '0.2 km').
max_distance.title: Max Distance

CrossingNotchConfig.description:
Cut the embankments of roads, railways and bridges out of the ground.

A DEM shows the embankment of a road across a valley as a wall: the flow
routing then fills behind it or digs through it, and the model top carries
the wall into the aquifer. The notch lowers the DEM along the channel at each
crossing to the bed level read on both sides of the structure, and nowhere
else. It is a correction of the ground: the routing chain and the model top
both start from the notched ground.

The notch follows the channel tree of ``[geographic.river_network]``, which
is delineated a first time on the ground, notched, and delineated again.
Weirs and dams are not notched: a weir is a drop of the bed, not a wall. A
road laid on a dam crest is not notched either: a crossing with a dam or a
weir of the file within ``snap_radius``, or a ``[geographic.enforce_lakes]``
polygon on its channel reach is left alone and reported as ``dam_or_weir``.

enabled.description: Notch the ground at the crossings of the channel tree with the declared structures, then delineate again on the notched ground. Needs [geographic.river_network] enabled.
enabled.title: Enabled

path.description: Vector file of the structures, with the columns 'kind', 'source', 'name' and 'drop_m' of the crossings data variable. When left empty and enabled, it is filled from [[data.crossings.sources]], so the structures are named once. Required when enabled, from one of the two.
path.title: Path

kinds.description: Structure kinds to notch. Weirs and dams are never notched.
kinds.title: Kinds

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

notch_width.description: Width of the notch across the embankment, in metres. The channel pixel itself is always lowered, so a width below the cell size cuts one pixel. The width is applied along the embankment only, the run of channel pixels that stand above the bed line, never to the two pixels where the bed is read. Accepts inline units (e.g. 10, '10 m').
notch_width.title: Notch Width

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

bed_reach.description: Distance along the channel, on each side of the crossing, where the bed level is read, in metres. The embankment is assumed narrower than twice this. The notch is the straight line between the two bed levels. A bed end that falls on the embankment of another crossing is read further along the channel, beyond it. Accepts inline units (e.g. 50, '50 m').
bed_reach.title: Bed Reach

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

max_depth.description: Largest lowering of any pixel, in metres. A pixel that would be lowered more is lowered by this and counted as capped in the report: the embankment is then higher than the cap allows for, or the crossing sits on a ridge. Accepts inline units (e.g. 3, '3 m').
max_depth.title: Max Depth

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

snap_radius.description: A point structure (a bridge of the ROE) farther than this from the channel tree is ignored, and so is a channel pixel farther than this from its crossing, in metres. A dam or a weir of the file within this distance of a crossing stops its notch. Accepts inline units (e.g. 30, '30 m').
snap_radius.title: Snap Radius

CutoffWallConfig.description: The flow barrier of a lake dam, laid on the lake shore.

enabled.description: Whether this barrier is built. Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
enabled.title: Enabled

auto.description: Auto-place the dam cutoff wall (lakes only): the trace is derived at bind time as the chord across the reservoir at its downstream neck (the footprint point nearest the catchment outlet), perpendicular to the outlet-flow direction. Mutually exclusive with line / line_path; the mesh dam refinement then follows this auto axis too.
auto.title: Auto

line.description: Inline barrier-trace vertices [(x, y), ...] in the project CRS. Mutually exclusive with line_path and auto.
line.title: Line

line_path.description: Barrier-trace file: a vector polyline (gpkg / shp / GeoJSON) or a CSV of ordered x,y (or lon,lat) vertices. A bare filename resolves against <workspace>/data/cutoff_wall/. Alternative to line and auto.
line_path.title: Line Path

depths.description: Barrier depth [m] below the top (or below crest_elevation). One value is uniform; several are interpolated per vertex along the trace. The HFB blocks every layer down to this depth. Mutually exclusive with base_elevation.
depths.title: Depths

crest_elevation.description: Absolute TOP elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]; defaults to the cell top (the DEM). Set it when the barrier crest sits below the DEM top. Not calibratable: raising the crest and lowering hydchr both shrink the flow section the wall lets through, so a search cannot tell the two apart. It is a built structure, not a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
crest_elevation.title: Crest Elevation

base_elevation.description: Absolute BOTTOM elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]. When set, the HFB spans [base_elevation, crest_elevation or top] and blocks EVERY layer in that band. Use it to make a full-height dam impervious: the concrete body plus the grout curtain block all flow from the crest down to the curtain foot (e.g. base_elevation = 41 m), so nothing seeps across the dam above that. Mutually exclusive with depths. Not calibratable: a deeper foot and a lower hydchr produce the same reduction of under-dam flow, so putting both in a search is equifinality by construction, the same mechanism that makes the second stage of the stream-network protocol pin the specific yield on its bound. When the foot is genuinely unknown, run mode = "comparison", one elevation per run, which also yields a defensible sensitivity instead of a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for an override.
base_elevation.title: Base Elevation

hydchr.description: HFB hydraulic characteristic [1/T] = K_barrier / thickness_barrier. A near-zero value (e.g. 1e-9 1/s) is a quasi-impermeable wall. Zero is accepted only without XT3D: MODFLOW 6 ignores a zero hydchr under XT3D, so the build refuses it with XT3D active (XT3D turns itself on for triangle and strongly non-orthogonal meshes). Each face of the barrier receives hydchr times trace length over the summed face length, so a zigzag chain of faces keeps the declared conductance. Mutually exclusive with k + thickness.
hydchr.title: Hydchr

hydchr_unit.description: Unit of hydchr (1/T): 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min. Converted to 1/s for MF6.
hydchr_unit.title: Hydchr Unit

k.description: Barrier hydraulic conductivity [L/T]. Give it with thickness in place of hydchr.
k.title: K

k_unit.description: Unit of k (L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h, m/min. Converted to m/s.
k_unit.title: K Unit

thickness.description: Thickness of the barrier, in the unit thickness_unit names (metres by default). With k it gives hydchr = k / thickness, in place of hydchr.
thickness.title: Thickness

thickness_unit.description: Unit of thickness (L): m, cm, mm, km. Converted to m.
thickness_unit.title: Thickness Unit

snap_tolerance.description: Largest gap [m] between the declared trace and the lake shore. The part of the trace facing the lake moves onto the shore it faces, so no cell sits between the reservoir and the wall; the trace beyond the banks stays as declared. A trace farther than this from the lake is refused. A trace that crosses the lake cuts its footprint, and the part downstream is dropped.
snap_tolerance.title: Snap Tolerance

Top-level ``[data]`` configuration for manager families.

The `types` list declares user-requested data families. The effective
active set can also include planner-inferred families deduced from other
sections (domain, flow) depending on `inference_mode`.

For each active type, the matching nested section can be validated dynamically:
- `geology` already uses its dedicated Pydantic model (`GeologyConfig`),
- `oceanic` uses `OceanicConfig`,
- the other data families are kept as validated mappings for now.

Use this model for validation only. Runtime activation order is represented
by ``DataLoadPlan`` and loaded by ``DataManagersRuntimeLoader``.

ExportRequest.description:
One export: what to write, when, in which format, where.

Only ``variables`` is required. ``time`` names instants and ``period`` a
window; without either the whole simulation is written. ``format`` is
optional: each data goes to its natural format (a field at one date to
GeoTIFF, over several dates to NetCDF, a series or a table to CSV, a vector
layer to GeoPackage, a raster layer to GeoTIFF), and a ``file`` extension
names the format too.

variables.description: What to export: a name, a list of names, or "all" for everything the run holds. One namespace covers the mesh fields (head, watertable_depth, seepage_mask..., and mesh_cell_area, which "all" leaves out because mesh_cells holds it), the series (discharge, discharge_obs...), the vector layers (watershed, hydrographic_network_reference...), the three layers of the cell mesh (mesh_cells, mesh_seeds, mesh_family_faces), the raster layers (watershed_dem...) and the table budget; 'hmp export <run> --list' prints what a run holds. A name no run can hold is refused before the solve.
variables.title: Variables

time.description: The instants to write: a date "YYYY-MM-DD", "first", "last", or a list of them. A date takes the stress period that holds it. A format that holds one instant (GeoTIFF, Shapefile, GeoPackage, VTU) writes one file per date. Left out, the whole simulation is written. Cannot be given with period.
time.title: Time

period.description: A window of the simulation, [start, end], two dates "YYYY-MM-DD". Every stress period it overlaps is written. Cannot be given with time.
period.title: Period

format.description: The file format. Left out, each data takes its natural format, or the one the extension of 'file' names. 'stac', 'rocrate' and 'prov' write the metadata of the run; those three describe the whole run and take variables = "all" only. The portable archive of a run is written by 'hmp publish --container tar'.

value_docs.csv: A CSV table (.csv): series and tables.
value_docs.geopackage: A GeoPackage vector file (.gpkg), one file per date. The mesh layers of a run share one file.
value_docs.geotiff: A GeoTIFF raster (.tif), one file per date.
value_docs.netcdf: A NetCDF file (.nc): fields and series over time.
value_docs.prov: The PROV provenance record of the run.
value_docs.rocrate: The RO-Crate metadata of the run.
value_docs.shapefile: An ESRI Shapefile (.shp), one file per date.
value_docs.stac: The STAC metadata of the run.
value_docs.vtu: A VTK unstructured grid (.vtu) of the mesh, one file per date.

folder.description: A folder under the exports/ directory of the run, where the files are written with automatic names. Relative to runs/<run>/exports/; an absolute folder or one that climbs out with '..' is refused. Left out, the files go to runs/<run>/exports/.
folder.title: Folder

file.description: One exact file to write; its extension gives the format. Relative to 'folder' under runs/<run>/exports/; an absolute file or one that climbs out with '..' is refused. Only for a request that writes one file: several files need 'folder' and automatic names.
file.title: File

crs.description: Output CRS, e.g. 'EPSG:4326'. Rasters and vector layers are reprojected from the model CRS. NetCDF, VTU and CSV do not reproject and refuse it. Left out, the model CRS is kept.
crs.title: Crs

resolution.description: Pixel size of a GeoTIFF of a field, in units of the output CRS. Left out, it is the side of the smallest cell of the mesh, and a mesh that would give more than 1e8 pixels is refused until a resolution is set. Refused on a request that writes no raster.

FlowBarrierConfig.description:
Typed payload for one MODFLOW 6 horizontal flow barrier (HFB).

The barrier is a quasi-impermeable vertical wall on a polyline. It sits on
the mesh faces laid on the trace (the ``barriers`` family of a triangle or
voronoi mesh), or on the faces the trace crosses (a regular grid), and spans
every top layer down to ``depths`` below the model top, so the flow is
blocked there and forced underneath. The dam cutoff wall is the lake-derived
use of this payload.

enabled.description: Whether this barrier is built. Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
enabled.title: Enabled

auto.description: Auto-place the dam cutoff wall (lakes only): the trace is derived at bind time as the chord across the reservoir at its downstream neck (the footprint point nearest the catchment outlet), perpendicular to the outlet-flow direction. Mutually exclusive with line / line_path; the mesh dam refinement then follows this auto axis too.
auto.title: Auto

line.description: Inline barrier-trace vertices [(x, y), ...] in the project CRS. Mutually exclusive with line_path and auto.
line.title: Line

line_path.description: Barrier-trace file: a vector polyline (gpkg / shp / GeoJSON) or a CSV of ordered x,y (or lon,lat) vertices. A bare filename resolves against <workspace>/data/cutoff_wall/. Alternative to line and auto.
line_path.title: Line Path

depths.description: Barrier depth [m] below the top (or below crest_elevation). One value is uniform; several are interpolated per vertex along the trace. The HFB blocks every layer down to this depth. Mutually exclusive with base_elevation.
depths.title: Depths

crest_elevation.description: Absolute TOP elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]; defaults to the cell top (the DEM). Set it when the barrier crest sits below the DEM top. Not calibratable: raising the crest and lowering hydchr both shrink the flow section the wall lets through, so a search cannot tell the two apart. It is a built structure, not a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
crest_elevation.title: Crest Elevation

base_elevation.description: Absolute BOTTOM elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]. When set, the HFB spans [base_elevation, crest_elevation or top] and blocks EVERY layer in that band. Use it to make a full-height dam impervious: the concrete body plus the grout curtain block all flow from the crest down to the curtain foot (e.g. base_elevation = 41 m), so nothing seeps across the dam above that. Mutually exclusive with depths. Not calibratable: a deeper foot and a lower hydchr produce the same reduction of under-dam flow, so putting both in a search is equifinality by construction, the same mechanism that makes the second stage of the stream-network protocol pin the specific yield on its bound. When the foot is genuinely unknown, run mode = "comparison", one elevation per run, which also yields a defensible sensitivity instead of a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for an override.
base_elevation.title: Base Elevation

hydchr.description: HFB hydraulic characteristic [1/T] = K_barrier / thickness_barrier. A near-zero value (e.g. 1e-9 1/s) is a quasi-impermeable wall. Zero is accepted only without XT3D: MODFLOW 6 ignores a zero hydchr under XT3D, so the build refuses it with XT3D active (XT3D turns itself on for triangle and strongly non-orthogonal meshes). Each face of the barrier receives hydchr times trace length over the summed face length, so a zigzag chain of faces keeps the declared conductance. Mutually exclusive with k + thickness.
hydchr.title: Hydchr

hydchr_unit.description: Unit of hydchr (1/T): 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min. Converted to 1/s for MF6.
hydchr_unit.title: Hydchr Unit

k.description: Barrier hydraulic conductivity [L/T]. Give it with thickness in place of hydchr.
k.title: K

k_unit.description: Unit of k (L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h, m/min. Converted to m/s.
k_unit.title: K Unit

thickness.description: Thickness of the barrier, in the unit thickness_unit names (metres by default). With k it gives hydchr = k / thickness, in place of hydchr.
thickness.title: Thickness

thickness_unit.description: Unit of thickness (L): m, cm, mm, km. Converted to m.
thickness_unit.title: Thickness Unit

FlowConfig.description:
Flow-process configuration.

Parameters are declared in `param_list` (ordered list of ids), and
parameter payloads are stored in `param`. A boundary or a sink is active when
it is declared and does not say ``enabled = false``: :attr:`active_bc` and
:attr:`active_sinks_sources` read that from the tables, and no list says it.

flow_regime.description: Whether the flow is solved as one equilibrium state or through time over the stress periods of [simulation.time].
flow_regime.title: Flow Regime

value_docs.steady: Solves one equilibrium state, with no storage term: one stress period over the whole [simulation.time] window, whatever its step_value says, with the forcings averaged over the window.
value_docs.transient: Solves the heads through time; it starts from the state [flow.ic] gives.

first_period_steady.description: For transient flow, mark the first solver stress period as steady-state. Ignored for steady flow, where all solver periods are steady.
first_period_steady.title: First Period Steady

restart_from.description: Optional hotstart: a prior run whose last time step seeds the initial heads (and the lake stage), overriding [flow.ic]. Name it by its run name, its sim_id, the path of its Zarr store, or the table {sim_id, path} the frozen config.toml of a run writes (the sim_id is looked up first, the path second). The prior run must share this run's mesh: a regular grid is rebuilt identically and a generated triangle or voronoi mesh is read back from the mesh cache of the project; otherwise the cell count differs and restart is refused. None keeps [flow.ic]. Read only by a solver that declares it can: elsewhere the run is refused rather than started from [flow.ic] without a word. This is one of the four ways to say where a transient starts, next to [flow.ic] kind='steady_state' (equilibrium under the mean recharge, or under a rate you state with source='prescribed'), kind='custom'/'top'/'bottom' (a level you write), and `hmp spinup` (repeat a representative window until the state stops moving, then point this key at its result).
restart_from.title: Restart From

param_list.description: Ordered list of the flow parameter ids the run builds, for example ['K', 'Ss', 'Sy']. Each id is described by its [flow.param.<id>] table.
param_list.title: Param List

param.description: Mapping of flow-parameter identifiers to native FieldParamConfig payloads.
param.title: Param

bc.description:
Mapping of flow boundary-condition payloads parsed from ``[flow.bc]``.

**Supported TOML sections**

- ``[flow.bc.<id>]``, one block per boundary, keyed by what it is. Canonical ids: ``drainage``, ``ocean``, ``stream``, ``north_side``, ``south_side``, ``east_side``, ``west_side``
- declaring a block is what activates the boundary, and ``enabled = false`` switches it off. An empty block is enough for a boundary the registry describes entirely, such as a drainage

**Common keys**

- ``kind``: optional, the registry supplies it: ``dirichlet`` for an imposed head, ``drain`` for the linear drain ``q = C (h - h_ref)``
- ``value``: optional on a drainage, where leaving it out derives the conductance from K; a head boundary with no value and no forcing builds no constant head
- ``application_domain``: optional, the registry supplies it, and a value contradicting it is refused

**Allowed application_domain values:** ``top``, ``north side``, ``south side``, ``east side``, ``west side``.

**Default units:** ``m`` for dirichlet, ``m2/s`` for drain.

**The drain under each solver:** the MODFLOW solvers build a ``DRN`` package. The Boussinesq solver takes its surface closure from ``flow.runtime.surface_interaction_model``.
bc.title: Bc

FlowEtpConfig.description:
Typed payload for diffuse evapotranspiration over the model domain.

Drives the MODFLOW EVT package. Conceptually parallel to
:class:`FlowRechargeConfig`: scalar / list / mapping / runtime-series
payloads are accepted and converted to SI ``m/s`` at runtime via
``apply_etp_load_result_to_flow``. The actual conversion to a
stress-period dictionary is handled by
:class:`FlowToModflowAdapter._build_etp_payload`. This is the unique
entry point for the EVT package.

enabled.description: Whether the model takes this evapotranspiration. Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
enabled.title: Enabled

values.description: Evapotranspiration rate, in the unit that units names (mm/day by default): one number, one number per stress period, a table {period: value}, or the series loaded from [data.etp]. Values must not be negative: the EVT package takes them as outflow rates.
values.title: Values

heterogeneous_source.description: Optional raw data source for heterogeneous (2D per-cell) ETP. When set, the solver adapter discretizes FieldRecords onto the MODFLOW grid instead of using the scalar 'values' field. Expected: LoadResult with FieldRecords.
heterogeneous_source.title: Heterogeneous Source

first_clim.description: ETP rate of every steady stress period, read by MODFLOW-NWT: every period of a steady run, and the first period of a transient run when flow.first_period_steady is true. 'mean' is the mean of the per-period rates, each weighted by its length; 'first' is the rate of period 0; a number is that rate. A transient period keeps its own rate.
first_clim.title: First Clim

units.description: Units of the ETP data source. Data-manager outputs use mm/day by convention; converted to m/s at runtime.
units.title: Units

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

surface_offset.description: Distance (m) the EVT surface sits below its reference. The rule has two cases. In soil mode under MODFLOW 6 the reference is the drain elevation of the cell (the top, or the top minus half of solver.drain_band_depth_m), and with the key unset the distance is 0 m, since the soil reservoir has already taken the ETP it could. In every other case the reference is the topographic surface, as MODFLOW-NWT reads it, and with the key unset the distance is 2 m, also when this table is absent and the ETP comes from [data.etp] alone. A value written here wins in both cases. The run writes the value it used in config.resolved.toml, table resolved_at_build.
surface_offset.title: Surface Offset

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

extinction_depth.description: Depth (m) below the EVT surface where the water table stops evaporating; the rate falls linearly between the surface and this depth. 2 m by default, a choice: this depth often reaches the deepest roots, and 150 mm of soil capacity means about 1 to 2 m of them. Read by MODFLOW-NWT, and by MODFLOW 6 in soil mode for the ETP the soil left unmet. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.extinction_depth]; the range belongs to the site, so a file has to state it.
extinction_depth.title: Extinction Depth

spatial_mode.description: How to interpret spatial data: 'auto' (points->homogeneous, fields->heterogeneous), 'homogeneous', or 'heterogeneous'.
spatial_mode.title: Spatial Mode

interpolation_method.description: How gridded or station data reach the cells of the solver mesh: 'nearest' (source value at the cell centre), 'linear', 'idw' (inverse distance), or 'area' (gridded data only: each pixel weighted by the area it shares with the cell, so the volume over the domain equals the integral of the grid).
interpolation_method.title: Interpolation Method

FlowICSpinupCyclic.description:
Initialize a transient run by repeating it until the state stops moving.

A steady solve carries the forcing's mean and nothing of its history, which is
the right start for an aquifer whose response time is short against the record.
It is the wrong one for a deep aquifer, or a lake whose storage integrates
several seasons: the state those reach depends on the sequence, not the average.

So the run's own period is repeated, each cycle starting from the head field the
previous one ended on, until the largest change between two cycles falls below
``tol_head``. The cycle is the simulated period itself rather than a window
chosen separately, which is what makes the antecedent consistent with the
forcing that is scored, and what lets a calibration trial use it: the cycles are
auxiliary solves inside one run, exactly as ``steady_state`` already is.

It costs one extra solve per cycle, per run. Inside a calibration that is per
trial, so a five-cycle spin-up multiplies a hundred-evaluation phase by six.

id.description: id of the initial condition (forced to 'h' for flow)
id.title: Id

value.description: Number the starting state reads, in metres: the head for kind 'custom', the depth below the top for kind 'top_offset'. The other kinds refuse it.
value.title: Value

description.description: Free text about the starting state, kept with the configuration. Unset, it reads "Initial condition 'h'".
description.title: Description

units.description: Runtime unit for the initial hydraulic-head field.
units.title: Units

kind.description: Repeat the simulated period, each cycle starting from the state the previous one ended on, until the head field stops moving.
kind.title: Kind

max_cycles.description: Most cycles the loop may run. A loop that runs out of cycles still hands back its last state and says so, rather than reporting a convergence that did not happen. A count.
max_cycles.title: Max Cycles

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

tol_head.description: Largest head change between two cycles that counts as settled, anywhere in the domain. One centimetre is a starting point; the honest check is to loosen it and see whether what you report moves.
tol_head.title: Tol Head

first_cycle_from.description: Where cycle one starts. 'top' is the water table at the surface, which the cycling then drains. 'steady_state' starts from the equilibrium under the mean forcing, which is closer and usually saves a cycle.
first_cycle_from.title: First Cycle From
