FlowLakeConfig.description:
Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 LAK lake.

The lake exchanges with the aquifer through its CONNECTIONDATA, parameterized
by ``bedleak`` (the lake-bed leakance, 1/T). ``initial_stage`` is the initial lake
stage. ``outlets`` declare the surverse / spillway / controlled releases; the
transient forcings (``rainfall`` and ``evaporation`` as rates L/T, ``runoff``,
``inflow`` and ``withdrawal`` as volumetric L^3/T) are optional runtime
declarations resolved against ``[simulation.time]``.

File references (geometry polygon, bathymetry raster, stage-volume-area
abacus, observed levels) are declared separately in the data layer.

enabled.description: Whether this lake is built. Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
enabled.title: Enabled

bedleak.description: Lake-bed leakance [1/T] = K_bed / thickness_bed. Resistance of the lake-aquifer interface over the whole lake bed, the handle of the lake-aquifer exchange. The flow through or under the dam is set by the cutoff_wall and the aquifer, not by this value. 0 means a perfectly sealed lakebed (no leakage).
bedleak.title: Bedleak

bedleak_unit.description: Unit of bedleak (leakance, 1/T): one of 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min (aliases like 1/d accepted). HydroModPy converts it to 1/s for MF6, so a 1/day leakance is not silently taken as 1/s.
bedleak_unit.title: Bedleak Unit

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

initial_stage.description: Lake stage at the start of the run: the elevation of the water surface, in metres.
initial_stage.title: Initial Stage

steady_stage_hold.description: Hold the lake stage at initial_stage during the steady warm-up period(s) (LAK status CONSTANT) and re-activate it on the first transient period. Use for a managed reservoir whose observed initial level is far from the natural steady equilibrium: the aquifer equilibrates around the observed stage instead of overriding it.
steady_stage_hold.title: Steady Stage Hold

occupied_layers.description: Number of top grid layers the lake occupies in each of its columns. 1 is a surface lake; a deeper reservoir embedded over several layers uses a higher count. Must leave at least one active layer below the lake for the VERTICAL leakage connection. A count of layers.
occupied_layers.title: Occupied Layers

fill_enclosed_cells.description: Fill cells enclosed by the lake footprint (the polygon's interior rings / islands) so the lake is contiguous. Off by default: interior rings stay active aquifer (real islands). Enable to drop sub-grid islands and classification pockets that would otherwise be isolated non-lake cells inside the lake.
fill_enclosed_cells.title: Fill Enclosed Cells

surfdep.description: LAK surface depression depth [L] that smooths the dry/wet (marnage) transition for Newton. Default (None) uses 0.1 m. Raise it (e.g. 0.5 to 1.0 m) to stabilise and speed up the active-littoral steady solve when many lakebed cells toggle at once; it slightly fuzzes the shoreline.
surfdep.title: Surfdep

bed_reconstruction.description: Optional bathymetry-driven bed carving. When set, the real lake bed is reconstructed from the lake_bathymetry raster (reconciled to the abacus) and carved into the grid instead of a flat reservoir.

outlets.description: Surverse / spillway / controlled-release outlets for this lake.

items.description: Discriminated union of lake outlet payloads (WEIR, MANNING, or SPECIFIED).

outlets.title: Outlets

cutoff_wall.description: Optional dam cutoff wall / grout curtain on the dam axis, modeled as a MODFLOW 6 HFB laid on the lake shore. The barrier forces the under-dam seepage to dive below the wall instead of leaking through the top layers. The flow across its faces is published per layer as the cutoff_wall_flow series.

anyOf.description: A quantity over the stress periods: 'constant', 'csv', 'piecewise' or 'seasonal'.

rainfall.description: Rainfall on the lake over time, as a rate per unit of lake surface (m/s in SI). It wins over the rainfall taken from [data.precipitation].
rainfall.title: Rainfall

anyOf.description: A quantity over the stress periods: 'constant', 'csv', 'piecewise' or 'seasonal'.

FlowLakeOutletMover.description:
A controlled LAK transfer for one outlet, routed through MVR.

The outlet keeps ``lakeout = 0`` (external) and this spec sends its discharge
to a receiver through a MODFLOW 6 MVR record. The receiver is one of ``lake``
(1-based downstream lake number, LAK -> LAK), ``reach`` (1-based downstream SFR
reach, LAK -> SFR spillway release), or ``to_downstream_reach`` (auto-resolve the
downstream reach on the mesh, robust to remeshing); exactly one must be set.
``mvrtype`` picks how much water moves: ``FACTOR`` (a fraction ``value`` of the
provider flow), ``UPTO`` (capped at ``value``), ``EXCESS`` (only above ``value``)
or ``THRESHOLD`` (all-or-nothing above ``value``).

lake.description: Number of the lake that receives the transfer, counted from 1 in the order the lakes are declared.
lake.title: Lake

reach.description: Number of the SFR reach that receives the transfer, counted from 1. A reach number changes when the mesh changes; to_downstream_reach does not.
reach.title: Reach

to_downstream_reach.description: Auto-resolve the LAK -> SFR receiver: route the spillway to the SFR reach on the foot of the dam, downstream of the cutoff wall when the lake has one. The SFR network draws a channel to the foot only with rectify_on_mesh; without a reach on the foot the build stops, it never takes the nearest reach, which can flow back into the lake. Robust to remeshing, unlike a fixed reach number. Keep lakeout = 0.
to_downstream_reach.title: To Downstream Reach

discharge_xy.description: Optional explicit spillway discharge point [x, y] in the project CRS. With to_downstream_reach, the dam foot is located nearest this point instead of inferred from the domain outlet. Use it when the spillway is not on the outlet-facing shore, or for a lake away from the catchment outlet.
discharge_xy.title: Discharge Xy

mvrtype.description: How much of the outlet flow the mover passes to the receiver, given value.
mvrtype.title: Mvrtype

value_docs.EXCESS: Moves only the part of the flow above value.
value_docs.FACTOR: Moves the share value (from 0 to 1) of the flow.
value_docs.THRESHOLD: Moves value once the flow exceeds it, and nothing below it.
value_docs.UPTO: Moves the flow, capped at value.

value.description: Amount of the transfer rule: a share from 0 to 1 for FACTOR, a flow rate in m3/s for UPTO, EXCESS and THRESHOLD.
value.title: Value

FlowReachNetworkConfig.description:
Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 SFR stream network.

The network is either traced automatically on A, the river network of
``[geographic.river_network]`` (whose threshold is the only one), or supplied
explicitly through ``reaches``.
Reaches exchange with the aquifer through their streambed conductance
(``streambed_k`` / ``streambed_thickness``) unless ``connected_to_aquifer`` is
False. The transient forcings (``headwater_inflow``, ``runoff`` as volumetric
L^3/T; ``rainfall``, ``evaporation`` as rates L/T) are optional runtime
declarations resolved against ``[simulation.time]``.

``outflow_to_lake`` is the only lake-aware field: when set, the terminal reach
feeds that lake (1-based) through an MVR record (SFR -> LAK). When None, the
network outflow leaves the model and SFR runs with no lake at all.

enabled.description: Whether this stream network is built. Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
enabled.title: Enabled

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

min_reach_length.description: Prune reaches shorter than this [L] (0 keeps all reaches).
min_reach_length.title: Min Reach Length

streambed_k.description: Streambed hydraulic conductivity rhk [L/T]. 0 = no reach-aquifer leakage (pure routing).
streambed_k.title: Streambed K

streambed_k_unit.description: Unit of streambed_k (velocity, L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h... HydroModPy converts it to m/s for MF6, so a m/day value is not taken as m/s.
streambed_k_unit.title: Streambed K Unit

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

min_slope.description: Smallest slope a reach bed may take, in metres of drop per metre (floor of rgrd). It also sets the drop the bed profile solve keeps between neighbouring reaches.
min_slope.title: Min Slope

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

bed_incision.description: Depth [L] of the streambed top rtp below the top of the reach's OWN aquifer cell. A bed never sits above the ground of its own cell, whether this is set or not. None (default) only lifts the lower bound: the bed may then sink to the cell bottom instead of stopping at max_bed_sag. When set, each reach is solved inside [cell_top - bed_incision - max_bed_sag, cell_top - bed_incision], monotone downstream, and the build refuses when that band is empty. rtp is delineated on the model top, so this anchors a bed that a coarse DEM cannot resolve; it is not a correction for the descent D, which never reaches the bed. Pick it against the water table, not against the channel: MODFLOW 6 switches a reach between connected and disconnected at rtp minus streambed_thickness (gwf-sfr.f90:3973-3985), so a bed sitting near the seasonal water-table depth toggles at every outer iteration.
bed_incision.title: Bed Incision

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

max_bed_sag.description: Only read when bed_incision is set. How far [L] below cell_top - bed_incision the monotone-downstream solve may sink a reach. It bounds the cumulative descent that a traced channel climbing over a rise forces on everything downstream of it. Widening it never refuses the build on its own: a reach that cannot hold the descent is warned about and pinned to the floor.
max_bed_sag.title: Max Bed Sag

width.description: How the reach width rwid [L] is set (constant / by_order / power_law).
width.title: Width

connected_to_aquifer.description: If False every reach uses cellid 'none' (routing only, no streambed leakage).
connected_to_aquifer.title: Connected To Aquifer

route_drainage.description: Route the hillslope drainage (DRN) discharge into the stream network: every remaining DRN cell of the basin hands its outflow, through an MVR record (FACTOR 1.0), to the first reach or lake cell met on its descent D, a filled copy of the model top. A cell whose descent leaves the model first keeps a plain DRN. This is the surface re-infiltration / runon convergence of drained water towards the river; without it only the reach cells' streambed captures baseflow and the rest of the catchment discharge is lost (a few per cent of the water of a catchment). On by default; set False only to study the network alone.
route_drainage.title: Route Drainage

storage.description: Enable the channel-storage term (transient first period / SIMPLE only).
storage.title: Storage

anyOf.description: A quantity over the stress periods: 'constant', 'csv', 'piecewise' or 'seasonal'.

headwater_inflow.description: Inflow from outside the model at the headwater reaches, as a volume per time (m3/s in SI).
headwater_inflow.title: Headwater Inflow

anyOf.description: A quantity over the stress periods: 'constant', 'csv', 'piecewise' or 'seasonal'.

runoff.description: Overland runoff that enters the network, as a volume per time (m3/s in SI), shared over the reaches by length.
runoff.title: Runoff

anyOf.description: A quantity over the stress periods: 'constant', 'csv', 'piecewise' or 'seasonal'.

rainfall.description: Rainfall on the channel surface, as a rate (m/s in SI).
rainfall.title: Rainfall

anyOf.description: A quantity over the stress periods: 'constant', 'csv', 'piecewise' or 'seasonal'.

evaporation.description: Evaporation from the channel surface, as a positive rate (m/s in SI) that is subtracted.
evaporation.title: Evaporation

reaches.description: Explicit reach table; bypasses delineation. None = trace the reaches on A, the river network.
reaches.title: Reaches

outflow_to_lake.description: Number of the lake the last reach feeds through a mover (SFR -> LAK), counted from 1 in the order the lakes are declared. Unset, the network outflow leaves the model.
outflow_to_lake.title: Outflow To Lake

outflow_mvrtype.description: How much of the network outflow the mover passes to the lake, given outflow_value.
outflow_mvrtype.title: Outflow Mvrtype

value_docs.EXCESS: Moves only the part of the outflow above outflow_value.
value_docs.FACTOR: Moves the share outflow_value (from 0 to 1) of the outflow.
value_docs.THRESHOLD: Moves outflow_value once the outflow exceeds it, and nothing below it.
value_docs.UPTO: Moves the outflow, capped at outflow_value.

outflow_value.description: Amount of the transfer rule: a share from 0 to 1 for FACTOR, a flow rate in m3/s for UPTO, EXCESS and THRESHOLD. Not calibratable: it is a coupling rule, not a hydraulic property of the reach or the lake, so letting a search move it would buy fit by reshaping how water is split between them rather than resolve streambed_k or the lake bathymetry, the actual unknowns. path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
outflow_value.title: Outflow Value

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

lake_feeder_snap.description: Max distance from a lake shoreline within which a dead-end reach is snapped to that lake via MVR (a real feeder the DEM fell short of). Scale it to the catchment: too large teleports an unrelated reach into the lake.
lake_feeder_snap.title: Lake Feeder Snap

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

outlet_keepout.description: Min distance from the model outlet a terminal reach must keep to count as a lake feeder. A terminal closer than this is the below-dam discharge reach (the lake feeds it and it leaves the model), so it is not routed into the lake.
outlet_keepout.title: Outlet Keepout

rectify_on_mesh.description: Re-derive the delineated reach cells as a clean single-flow-direction (SFD) channel on the DISV mesh. From every delineated cell the descent D, a filled copy of the model top, is traced one neighbour at a time until it reaches a lake, the outlet of D, or an already-traced cell. The union of those paths is the channel: one cell wide (a single downstream per cell, so no braiding), continuous on the descent graph (shared faces, or shared nodes on a quad mesh), following the thalweg of D (so the surface flow follows the reach), and always reaching a real sink (no inland dead-end that leaks its flow out). The streambed top is read on the model top, never on D. D is a copy and never returns to the solver.
rectify_on_mesh.title: Rectify On Mesh

rectify_stub_max_upstream.description: When rectify_on_mesh is set, demote a low-order parallel stub to hillslope drainage (DRN -> SFR) to thin braided bands: a reach cell with at most this many reach cells upstream of it that runs beside a reach carrying strictly more (the true channel) is dropped from SFR, keeping a one-thread channel; its water still reaches the network as routed drainage. 0 demotes only headwater leaves, a negative value keeps every traced cell. Default 2 removes stubs up to ~3 cells.
rectify_stub_max_upstream.title: Rectify Stub Max Upstream

rectify_min_component_cells.description: When rectify_on_mesh is set, drop a whole reach component smaller than this many cells (a lone one-cell stream that just touches a lake or the outlet is hillslope drainage, not a channel, and reads as a spurious SFR -> lake entry). Its water still reaches the network as routed DRN. Default 2 drops single-cell components; 1 keeps every component.
rectify_min_component_cells.title: Rectify Min Component Cells

FlowRechargeConfig.description:
Typed payload for diffuse recharge over the model domain.

Recharge drives RCHA under MODFLOW 6, RCH under MODFLOW-NWT and the recharge
term of the residual under Boussinesq. Each solver builds its own
stress-period data from this payload. Negative values can be routed to EVT
when ``negative_to_evt`` is enabled, under the two MODFLOW solvers only.

Attributes
----------
values :
    Recharge payload. Accepted forms:

    - **scalar** ``float``: uniform rate applied to every stress period,
    - **list / numpy array**: one value per stress period
      (length must match ``nper``),
    - **mapping** ``{period_index: value}``: one value for every stress
      period, the keys counted from 0,
    - **runtime series** (pandas-like object with ``.iloc``): used when
      recharge is computed dynamically (e.g. from PyHELP output).

first_clim : str | float
    Rate of every steady stress period, taken from the rates of all the
    periods (``hydromodpy.physics.forcing.steady_periods``). A transient
    period keeps its own rate. Options:

    - ``"mean"``: time mean of the per-period rates, each weighted by its length
      (default),
    - ``"first"``: rate of period 0,
    - *numeric*: that rate.

units : str
    Physical units of ``values``. The flow runtime converts the payload
    to SI ``m/s`` when the process is built.

enabled.description: Whether the model receives this recharge. Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
enabled.title: Enabled

values.description: Recharge rate: one number, one number per stress period, or a table {period: value} that states every period, in the unit that 'units' names (mm/day by default). It is positive when water enters the aquifer; a negative rate leaves it, through the EVT package when negative_to_evt holds. A calibration reads its bounds in that unit too. Do not write it beside [data.recharge] or the soil section, which replace it.
values.title: Values

factor.description: Number that multiplies the recharge in force, from 'values' or from [data.recharge], a deficit and a numeric first_clim included. 1 changes nothing. Do not write it beside the soil section, whose recharge is an output.
factor.title: Factor

soil.description: Soil reservoir that computes the recharge from the daily precipitation and ETP loaded under [data.precipitation] and [data.etp], MODFLOW 6 only. It replaces [data.recharge]. Check it alone with `hmp run <file> --until load_data`, which prints its water budget in mm/year and writes no run.

heterogeneous_source.description: Optional raw data source for heterogeneous (2D per-cell) recharge. When set, the solver adapter discretizes FieldRecords onto the MODFLOW grid instead of using the scalar 'values' field. Expected: LoadResult with FieldRecords.
heterogeneous_source.title: Heterogeneous Source

first_clim.description: Recharge rate of every steady stress period: every period of a steady run, and the first period of a transient run when flow.first_period_steady is true. 'mean' is the mean of the per-period rates, each weighted by its length; 'first' is the rate of period 0; a number is that rate, in the units of values. A transient period keeps its own rate. The same rule holds for one value per period and for one grid per period, under every solver. With negative_to_evt, the steady period takes the rule on the recharge part and on the deficit part, so its net rate is the one stated here. Boussinesq has no EVT and refuses a negative number.
first_clim.title: First Clim

units.description: Unit of 'values' and of the recharge data source. Data-manager outputs use mm/day by convention; set it when you write 'values' in another unit. The run converts the rate to m/s.
units.title: Units

negative_to_evt.description: When true, negative recharge values are routed to the solver EVT package and RCH receives the non-negative clipped recharge. Boussinesq has no EVT and refuses a negative rate whatever this says.
negative_to_evt.title: Negative To Evt

spatial_mode.description: How to interpret spatial data: 'auto' (points->homogeneous, fields->heterogeneous), 'homogeneous' (force spatial averaging), 'heterogeneous' (force per-cell discretization, including point-to-grid interpolation when stations have coordinates).
spatial_mode.title: Spatial Mode

interpolation_method.description: How gridded or station data reach the cells of the solver mesh: 'nearest' (source value at the cell centre), 'linear', 'idw' (inverse distance), or 'area' (gridded data only: each pixel weighted by the area it shares with the cell, so the volume over the domain equals the integral of the grid).
interpolation_method.title: Interpolation Method

FlowRechargeConfig.title: FlowRechargeConfig

^.+__delete$.description: Remove the inherited key. Only the literal true is accepted.

FlowRuntimeConfig.description: How the Boussinesq solver runs its nonlinear solve.

backend.description: Engine the Boussinesq solver uses for its nonlinear solve. 'local' and 'scipy' build a dense matrix and run on at most 400 cells; 'scipy_sparse' and 'petsc' (it needs petsc4py) have no such limit. 'auto' runs 'local' up to 400 cells and 'scipy_sparse' above, and logs the choice. The MODFLOW solvers do not read it.
backend.title: Backend

surface_interaction_model.description: Optional Boussinesq surface-interaction closure selector. 'regularized_partition' uses the Marcais-style q_ex = G_r(theta) R(balance) law; 'complementarity' uses the mixed PETSc q_ex-perp-(z_top-h) formulation; 'vi_obstacle' uses the PETSc head-only VI obstacle formulation, and 'ts_vi_obstacle' the same one integrated by PETSc TS; 'auto' keeps the historical backend-dependent default.
surface_interaction_model.title: Surface Interaction Model

partition_release_depth_m.description: Depth scale, in metres, of the regularized partition, the surface closure the Boussinesq solver uses by default on every engine but petsc. A cell whose water table lies d metres below the land surface releases at the surface the share exp(-d / depth) of the water it receives, its lateral inflow plus its recharge and wells: all of it with the water table at the surface, 37 % at one depth scale, 2e-9 at 1 m with the default 0.05 m. It stands for the microtopography over which seepage starts, and smooths the onset of seepage for the Newton solve. A smaller value comes closer to the exact threshold of the complementarity closure and makes the solve stiffer. The other closures and the MODFLOW solvers do not read it.

GeographicConfig.description:
Geographic configuration for watershed delineation.

This model stores parameters used to extract and prepare the physical domain
(watershed geometry and rasters) based on various possible input definitions.

Standard mode uses an external DEM with one of the catchment definitions:
direct DEM, XYZ text grid, outlet coordinate, or polygon shapefile.
Synthetic mode builds an analytical support and bypasses external DEM
delineation.

source_mode.description: Where the model domain comes from. 'standard' delineates it from a DEM, an outlet or a polygon ([geographic.catchment]). 'synthetic' builds one analytical support from [geographic.synthetic].
source_mode.title: Source Mode

anyOf.description: Catchment definition discriminator.

catchment.description: How the model domain is defined. Required when source_mode='standard', left out when it is 'synthetic'. The shape is chosen by 'kind' on the nested table: 'dem' | 'txt' | 'from_outlet_coord' | 'from_polyg_shp'.
catchment.title: Catchment

crs_project.description: Target projected CRS for all outputs (e.g. 'EPSG:2154'). If not set, derived from the input DEM.
crs_project.title: Crs Project

dem_correc_type.description: How the DEM is conditioned before the catchment is delineated. 'fill' (default) only raises cells: each closed depression is raised to its spill level, then a small gradient on the flats lets every cell drain. 'breach' mostly lowers cells: it carves a path through the barrier that closes a depression, after raising single-cell pits to their lowest neighbour, with no limit on length or depth and no fill afterwards (least-cost breaching, Lindsay 2016); it changes far fewer cells than 'fill' and can dig deep. 'capped_breach' lowers and raises: it breaches only within the limits of [geographic.capped_breach] (a maximum cumulative lowering and a maximum length, in metres), then fills every depression the limits refused (the hybrid of Lindsay 2016). The depth limit is a sum over the cells of a path, so it does not give the same landscape at every grid resolution. 'fill' is the default because it is the tool of the paper behind the network criterion (FillDepressions, Abherve et al. 2023), and the criterion itself fills the model top on the mesh by a priority flood: one conditioning rule from the DEM to the score.
dem_correc_type.title: Dem Correc Type

capped_breach.description: Limits of the 'capped_breach' conditioning: max_depth (default 0.5 m) and max_distance (default 200 m). Omitted, a 'capped_breach' run uses those defaults. Declaring it with any other dem_correc_type is refused: 'fill' and 'breach' have no limit to set, and a section that is silently ignored reads as a limit that was applied.

terrain_engine.description: Flow-routing engine that conditions the DEM and delineates the catchment. Unset uses the engine this build defaults to. A string and not an enumeration: the values that resolve depend on what is installed beside HydroModPy, which is how a third-party engine is named without a patch.
terrain_engine.title: Terrain Engine

domain_extent.description: Selects the DEM surface used for the domain. 'box' (default) keeps the full buffered rectangular support. 'watershed' / 'watershed_buff' select the catchment (optionally with a buffer ring) surface. Note: the MODFLOW 6 mesh still covers the buffered box (the buffer stays active for inter-basin exchange); out-of-watershed drainage is kept out of the catchment discharge by the DRN watershed-routing, not by an idomain mask.
domain_extent.title: Domain Extent

reg_fold.description: Folder with pre-computed regional flow rasters. When set, rasters are loaded instead of recomputed.
reg_fold.title: Reg Fold

synthetic.description: Synthetic geographic support used when source_mode='synthetic'. This analytical mode bypasses watershed delineation from external DEM files.

river_network.description: Optional DEM-derived river-network extraction settings. When disabled, no stream network is generated in geographic preprocessing.

enforce_lakes.description: Optional lake footprint polygons that the crossing notch and the bed regularisation leave alone. The routing DEM is not carved at the lakes.

crossings.description: Optional notch of the ground at the roads, railways and bridges that cross the generated channel tree: the embankment is lowered to the bed level read on both sides, and the catchment is delineated again on the notched ground.

bed_regularization.description: Optional least-change regularisation of the channel bed in the model top, on the pixels of the generated channel tree: the bed never rises downstream, crossing notches are gaps and declared weirs are drops.

dam_buffer.description: Base half-width, in metres, of the structure refinement corridors; also the radius of the optional dam-outlet disk.

MatchingHydrographicNetworkOptions.description:
What a file may say about the protocol beyond naming it.

Every default here is the value of the publication or a departure the protocol
declares and prints (``Deviation``). The names are the ones the file uses for
its own parameters and outputs, and the engines are free: the method is the
pair of criteria and the order they run in, not the optimizer that walks them.

name.description: Name of the protocol to run. 'matching_hydrographic_network' is the only one: a steady stage fits K on the stream network, then a transient stage fits the storage on a gauge.
name.title: Name

version.description: Recipe version this file was written against. Unset runs the version this installation carries. Pinned, the file runs what that version writes for every key of the network output it leaves empty, so a result that informed a decision stays replayable. A version the installation no longer carries is refused rather than approximated.
version.title: Version

conductivity.description: Name of the calibration parameter stage one moves, as the file declares it under [calibration.parameters].
conductivity.title: Conductivity

storage.description: Name of the calibration parameter stage two moves. false runs the network stage alone, which is a method in its own right: it identifies the conductivity without any discharge record.
storage.title: Storage

network_output.description: Name of the network output stage one is scored on. Unset picks the single output declared with support='network'.
network_output.title: Network Output

steady_metric.description: Criterion of stage one. 'distance_gap' is the signed difference of Eq. 1, whose zero is the balance the paper solves for. 'distance_mean' is the mean offset: a diagnostic, and the estimator of the reference script, whose interior minimum sits nowhere in particular.
steady_metric.title: Steady Metric

steady_method.description: Engine of stage one. The signed criterion crosses zero once over several decades, which is what a root search wants; any registered engine is accepted.
steady_method.title: Steady Method

anyOf.description: Positive integer.

steady_max_trials.description: Evaluation budget of stage one. 'auto' lets an engine that counts its evaluations size it: the bisection budgets its worst case, S + 2E + ceil(log2(1 / t)) for a root found after its E bracket expansions, 23 on [1e-7, 1e-3] m/s with seven sweep points and one per cent; any other engine gets 100. A number below the bisection's nominal count, S + ceil(log2(s / t)) for a root inside the bounds (15 there), is refused before the first solve.

steady_method_options.description: Options of the stage-one method, named as that method names them: for the bisection, sweep_points, bracket_expand, rel_tol and signed_component. value_docs.distance_gap: Balances the simulated stream network against the mapped one; zero marks the crossing.
value_docs.distance_mean: Mean spatial offset between simulated and mapped streams; a diagnostic, not a substitute for distance_gap.
value_docs.kge: Kling-Gupta efficiency, 2009 form (bias as the ratio of sums, variability as the ratio of standard deviations); separates correlation, variability and bias when NSE alone is ambiguous.
value_docs.mae: Mean absolute error, in the observed unit; less sensitive to outliers than RMSE.
value_docs.nse: Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency against the observed mean; the standard choice for a level or discharge series.
value_docs.nse_delta: NSE on the increments of the series rather than its level; a level is an integral and can hide flux errors that compensate, which only its increments show.
value_docs.nse_log: NSE on log-transformed series; weights low flows as heavily as peaks, good for recessions.
value_docs.nse_seasonal: NSE against the seasonal cycle rather than the overall mean; asks whether the model beats climatology.
value_docs.reservoir: Half nse_seasonal plus half nse_delta, built for an impounded level: a plain NSE there is beaten by the seasonal cycle, and the increments are what carry the flux errors.
value_docs.rmse: Root-mean-square error, in the observed unit; penalizes large misfits most.

Modflow6RuntimeConfig.description: Expert runtime settings used to build and solve MODFLOW 6 packages.

mf6_executable_name.description: MODFLOW 6 executable name or absolute path.
mf6_executable_name.title: Mf6 Executable Name

ims_print_option.description: IMS PRINT_OPTION. 'SUMMARY' adds one line per time step to the listing with the outer and inner iteration counts, which is the only way to tell an expensive iteration from too many of them. Deliberately NOT tied to mf_verbose: that switch also sets print_input and print_flows on the whole model, and on a run with one drain per cell those print every boundary flux at every step. 'NONE' by default; 'SUMMARY' costs a line per step.
ims_print_option.title: Ims Print Option

print_head.description: Re-print the whole head field, formatted as text, into the model listing at every output step. Nothing in the package reads it, and the binary head file already carries the same numbers. It costs DISK, not time: on a 25 m mesh of about 240 000 cells, 1826 daily steps wrote a listing of about 3 GB, but a one-variable-at-a-time probe put its effect on the solve at -0.4 per cent, inside the noise. Default false to stop producing the file, not to go faster. The listing keeps its budget summaries and its convergence reports either way, and Mf6ListBudget reads those.
print_head.title: Print Head

save_specific_discharge.description: Compute and write the cell-by-cell Darcy velocity (DATA-SPDIS). Required by particle tracking and by any velocity figure. The cost is the COMPUTATION, not the write: MODFLOW interpolates a velocity vector per cell at every step. Measured by changing this switch alone on a 25 m mesh of about 240 000 cells, it is about a fifth of the solve. A calibration that only scores a discharge series should turn it off.
save_specific_discharge.title: Save Specific Discharge

save_saturation.description: Compute and write the cell saturation (DATA-SAT). Measured by changing this switch alone on a 25 m mesh of about 240 000 cells, it is about a tenth of the solve. Same reasoning as save_specific_discharge: the cost is the per-cell computation, and the two together are worth about a third.
save_saturation.title: Save Saturation

mf6_runner.description: MODFLOW 6 solve dispatch: 'subprocess' runs the mf6 executable, 'api' drives libmf6 via the optional modflowapi package. Both write the same simulation, so output extraction is identical.
mf6_runner.title: Mf6 Runner

anyOf.description: Positive floating-point value.

mf6_api_timeout_s.description: Wall-clock budget (seconds) of one trial of a parallel calibration, whichever runner solves it; its worker is killed past it so one stuck trial cannot wedge the session. None keeps the built-in default (14400 s).
mf6_api_timeout_s.title: Mf6 Api Timeout S

mf6_ims_complexity.description: IMS complexity preset for MODFLOW 6: SIMPLE, MODERATE, or COMPLEX.
mf6_ims_complexity.title: Mf6 Ims Complexity

mf_verbose.description: Enable verbose FloPy logging for MODFLOW 6 setup and execution.
mf_verbose.title: Mf Verbose

mf6_outer_maximum.description: Maximum number of IMS outer iterations.
mf6_outer_maximum.title: Mf6 Outer Maximum

mf6_inner_maximum.description: Maximum number of IMS inner iterations.
mf6_inner_maximum.title: Mf6 Inner Maximum

anyOf.description: Positive floating-point value.

mf6_inner_rclose.description: IMS inner-iteration flow-residual closure (L^3/T in run units). None keeps the complexity-preset default.
mf6_inner_rclose.title: Mf6 Inner Rclose

mf6_backtracking_number.description: IMS residual-reduction backtracking: maximum number of backtracking steps tried per outer iteration (BACKTRACKING_NUMBER). Zero turns backtracking off. None keeps the complexity-preset default (20 for COMPLEX). Backtracking can stall the outer loop when a boundary package feeds flow back to another (DRN to MVR to SFR); setting 0 then often converges faster.
mf6_backtracking_number.title: Mf6 Backtracking Number

mf6_linear_acceleration.description: IMS linear acceleration: CG for symmetric matrices, BICGSTAB for the non-symmetric Newton formulation. None keeps the preset default.
mf6_linear_acceleration.title: Mf6 Linear Acceleration

anyOf.description: Positive integer.

mf6_preconditioner_levels.description: IMS ILUT fill: entries kept per row of each incomplete factor. A fill as wide as the matrix band, with a zero drop tolerance, gives a complete factorization. None keeps the preset default (5 for COMPLEX).
mf6_preconditioner_levels.title: Mf6 Preconditioner Levels

mf6_preconditioner_drop_tolerance.description: IMS ILUT drop tolerance: factor entries below it are dropped. Zero keeps every entry the fill allows. None keeps the preset default (1e-4 for COMPLEX).
mf6_preconditioner_drop_tolerance.title: Mf6 Preconditioner Drop Tolerance

mf6_reordering_method.description: IMS REORDERING_METHOD: order of the matrix rows before the incomplete factorization. 'rcm' is reverse Cuthill-McKee, which narrows the band; 'md' is minimum degree, which limits the fill. 'none' keeps the cell numbering of the mesh and writes nothing to the IMS file. The ordering changes the preconditioner, so the iteration count and the time, not the converged heads beyond the closure criteria. Measured on Voronoi DISV meshes of 14 400 to 144 000 cells, with a shuffled or a row-sorted numbering, and on a steady Flume solve of 73 400 cells, 'rcm' and 'md' never cut the inner iterations (3 to 73 per cent more), and the time did not drop beyond the noise of a loaded machine.
mf6_reordering_method.title: Mf6 Reordering Method

mf6_under_relaxation.description: IMS non-linear under-relaxation scheme. DBD is recommended with Newton. None keeps the preset default.
mf6_under_relaxation.title: Mf6 Under Relaxation

mf6_enable_rewet.description: Enable NPF cell rewetting. When left to None, HydroModPy keeps rewetting disabled unless explicitly enabled.
mf6_enable_rewet.title: Mf6 Enable Rewet

mf6_newton.description: Enable the MODFLOW 6 Newton-Raphson formulation. Catchment cells are always convertible (unconfined), so Newton with under-relaxation is the robust default. Unlike MODFLOW-NWT, it builds the horizontal conductance from the full cell thickness times the upstream saturation. The grid MODFLOW 6 reads therefore has a computational top that gives every cell of the top layer the same thickness, so that this conductance is the one of NWT; the ground stays in every package and in the run store.
mf6_newton.title: Mf6 Newton

mf6_newton_under_relaxation.description: Enable MODFLOW 6 Newton under-relaxation when mf6_newton is true.
mf6_newton_under_relaxation.title: Mf6 Newton Under Relaxation

mf6_ats.description: Enable MODFLOW 6 adaptive time stepping (ATS) on transient periods. Each period starts at the step simulation.time.substeps_per_period asked for and MF6 subdivides below it only where the solver cannot converge (e.g. littoral wet/dry under Newton); it never grows past that step, so turning ATS on cannot coarsen a run. When on, OC saves per period end so the extraction still sees one record per period. Default off (baseline).
mf6_ats.title: Mf6 Ats

mf6_ats_dtmin_s.description: Minimum ATS time step in seconds (only used when mf6_ats is true).
mf6_ats_dtmin_s.title: Mf6 Ats Dtmin S

mf6_enable_xt3d.description: Enable MF6 NPF XT3D terms. When left to None, XT3D turns on where a consistent result needs it, with a RuntimeWarning: a tilted K tensor (a non-zero flow parameter angle2 or angle3, which MF6 reads only under XT3D), and a K22 different from K on a cell whose angle1 is not a multiple of 90 degrees, or anywhere on an unstructured mesh. Without XT3D the two-point flux drops the cross terms of such a tensor, and the head error does not shrink with refinement. XT3D also turns on, with an INFO log, on triangle cells and on a significantly non-orthogonal mesh. A structured grid with K along its axes, or an orthogonal mesh with K22 equal to K, keeps it off. XT3D costs from about 1.5 times the MF6 run time on one layer to about 10 times on ten layers. true turns it on without a warning; false turns it off, with a RuntimeWarning when a consistent result needs it.
mf6_enable_xt3d.title: Mf6 Enable Xt3D

mf6_rewet_wetdry.description: MF6 NPF WETDRY threshold used when rewetting is active.
mf6_rewet_wetdry.title: Mf6 Rewet Wetdry

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

dem_resolution.description: Cell size the DEM is aggregated to before anything is delineated, a length ('75 m', a bare number in metres). The routing surface, the catchment, the mesh and the model top all take it. Unset keeps the pixel of the DEM file, which is what the mesh follows otherwise: 25 m for a BD ALTI download. Second of three sizes, each read from the one before: data.dem.sources.resolution_m says what a provider serves, this key what the run works on, and mesh.cell_size what the model solves on. Aggregation only: each coarse cell is the mean of the fine pixels it covers, nodata left out, on a grid aligned on the upper-left corner of the DEM; a value finer than the DEM's own pixel is refused when the run starts. The DEM file is not changed, the aggregated copy lives in the geographic products of the run.
dem_resolution.title: Dem Resolution

kind.description: Watershed delineated from outlet coordinates on a regional DEM.
kind.title: Kind

x_outlet.description: Easting of the watershed outlet in the projected CRS of the project, in meters.
x_outlet.title: X Outlet

y_outlet.description: Northing of the watershed outlet in the projected CRS of the project, in meters.
y_outlet.title: Y Outlet

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

snap_dist.description: Width (metres) of the square window the outlet is moved inside, centred on the declared coordinate. Not a maximum displacement: the window reaches floor(snap_dist / (2 * cell size)) cells on each side, so a value equal to the cell size moves nothing, and 150 m on a 25 m grid reaches 3 cells, 75 m. snap_method says where the outlet lands in the window. Accepts inline units (e.g. 50, '50 m', '0.05 km').
snap_dist.title: Snap Dist

snap_method.description: Where the outlet lands inside the window of snap_dist. 'window' (default) takes the cell with the largest flow accumulation, so it can land on a larger stream that lies in the window beside the one the outlet was declared on. 'jenson' takes the nearest cell of the stream network drawn from the DEM (Jenson and Domingue 1988, as used by Lindsay, Rothwell and Davies 2008), so it stays on the nearest stream, and it refuses an outlet with no stream cell in its window. The network is the cells that drain more than the threshold of [geographic.river_network] (threshold_area_km2 in km^2, or threshold_cells), which 'jenson' needs even when that section is not enabled. It is computed from the DEM: no observed network is read.
snap_method.title: Snap Method

buff_area.description: Margin around the watershed polygon. A percentage ('10%') enlarges the catchment AREA by that share, the rule of Abherve et al. (2023): the distance is solved on the real polygon, then snapped to the DEM grid. A length ('500 m', '2 km') is an explicit distance, snapped to the DEM grid like the percentage. '10% of sqrt(area)' is the rule of version 1 written out, 10 per cent of the square root of the catchment area, about 50 per cent more area on a real catchment. A bare number (10) still reads as that rule and warns, so a sealed run replays its domain; hmp doctor --fix-config rewrites it in the explicit form with the same distance.
buff_area.title: Buff Area

PersistenceConfig.description:
Orthogonal switch governing every persistence sink.

Toggles are independent: disabling ``save_zarr`` does not silence the
catalog, and vice versa. ``save_catalog`` is the master switch for the
project DuckDB; when False, every write through
:class:`Catalog` becomes a no-op.

save_catalog.description: Persist DuckDB rows (simulations, parameters, metrics, calibration_iterations). When False, catalog writes are skipped.
save_catalog.title: Save Catalog

save_zarr.description: Persist per-simulation field arrays (head, concentration, derived) into the Zarr store.
save_zarr.title: Save Zarr

field_precision.description: Precision of the time-varying field arrays of fields.zarr: heads, per-cell budget terms, derived fields, concentrations. 'compact' stores float32 with the mantissa rounded to nearest at 16 bits: each value moves by at most 2**-17 of itself (7.6e-6 relative, so at most 1 mm on a 130 m head and 7.6e-9 m3/s on a 1e-3 m3/s cell flux), and a daily run takes about a third of the disk. 'exact' keeps every value as computed, float64. Mesh geometry, topography, layer thickness, indices, coordinates and timestamps are never rounded.
field_precision.title: Field Precision

save_parquet.description: Persist per-simulation tabular outputs (timeseries, budgets, mass_balance) as Parquet files.
save_parquet.title: Save Parquet

compression.description: Codec DECLARED for Zarr field arrays and Parquet tables. The writers carry their own codec (zstd) and do not read this field, so changing it changes nothing today; it records the intent and is the field a writer would read once the choice is threaded through.
compression.title: Compression

compression_level.description: Compression level DECLARED for those writers. Same as the codec: core/io/parquet.py and core/io/geoparquet.py hold level 5 and do not read this field. The default says 5 rather than 3 so the declaration at least matches the bytes actually written.
compression_level.title: Compression Level

ResultsConfig.description:
Configuration for ``[simulation.results]``.

Controls whether simulation outputs are stored in the Catalog, which raw
solver files are kept and how much of the per-cell budget a run keeps.
Every derived field is rebuilt on read. Automated export formats live in
the top-level ``[export]`` section (:class:`ExportConfig`), not here.

keep_solver_files.description: Keep the raw solver files (.hds, .cbc, .lst) of a sealed run under runs/<run>/solver/, outside the manifest inventory. Off, they are deleted once their results are stored.
keep_solver_files.title: Keep Solver Files

keep_per_cell_budget.description: Keep every per-cell budget term the solver produces, storage terms included, so every flux can be mapped, exported and read after the run is sealed (hmp export, hmp viz show, the Python API), and every derived field is rebuilt on read. False keeps only the terms the run's own consumers read: the figures of [display].figures, the [[export]] blocks, the calibration criterion and the seepage mask of a surface-excess solver. A later read of anything else then needs a new run. On a daily run, true is the heaviest group of the store: about 300 MB for six daily years on about 21 000 cells, 3.7 times the head.
keep_per_cell_budget.title: Keep Per Cell Budget

step_value.description: Forcing/stress-period time-step scalar or inline token '<value> <unit>' (for example '30 day'). This controls the temporal aggregation step for forcing series (for example recharge/runoff) and the resulting stress periods. Not read by a steady run (flow.flow_regime = 'steady'), which is one stress period over the whole window, its forcings averaged over it.
step_value.title: Step Value

step_unit.description: Unit of a bare-number step_value: the length of the stress periods and of the forcing steps.
step_unit.title: Step Unit

value_docs.day: Treats step_value as whole days, the common granularity for daily forcing series.
value_docs.hour: Treats step_value as whole hours, for sub-daily forcing and stress periods.
value_docs.month: Treats step_value as calendar months, so the step length varies by month.
value_docs.year: Treats step_value as calendar years, so the step length varies with leap years.

substeps_per_period.description: Number of solver time steps within each stress period, the one knob that buys transient accuracy. The default of 1 integrates a whole period in a single backward-Euler step, which is not a neutral choice: on a seasonally recharged hillslope drained by DRN cells it moves the monthly discharge by 4 to 28 % against a refined run, across the whole plausible bedrock range, and a calibration scored on discharge absorbs that into the fitted parameters. The right count compares the aquifer response time `tau = L^2 S / (K b)` with the period length, and the solver cost is linear in it; 30 gives daily steps inside monthly periods. Consumed by the MODFLOW backends as DIS NSTP / TDIS nstp, and by the Boussinesq backend, which solves each period in as many backward-Euler steps of equal length. Every solver stores one result per period: the head at the end of the period and each flux as the mean of its steps, weighted by their length.

coverage_policy.description: What happens to a stress period that a forcing record does not cover. SoilReservoirConfig.description:
Daily soil reservoir that turns precipitation and ETP into recharge.

Read by the recharge binder of every run and of every calibration trial;
MODFLOW 6 only. See ``physics/hydrology/soil_reservoir/kernel.py`` for the
equations.

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

ru.description: Available water capacity of the soil, in mm of water: what the roots can draw between field capacity and wilting point. A bare number is in mm; "120 mm" and "12 cm" also read. Between 0 and 1000 mm. Required, since it belongs to the site. Start from a soil map, then compare the recharge the soil alone prints for 50 to 250 mm with the gauged discharge (hmp run <file> --until load_data). With [data.soil_capacity], it is the mean capacity over the catchment, and the raster spreads it over classes inside each cell. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.ru].
ru.title: Ru

alpha.description: Share of ru above which the soil evaporates at the full rate kc x ETP. Below alpha x ru, ETR falls linearly with the stored water. It is 1 - p of FAO-56 and LP of HBV. The default 0.45 is a choice: it means p = 0.55, the value of FAO-56 table 22 for cereals and maize (pasture 0.60). Above 0, at most 1. Kept fixed by default: on the discharge alone it trades off with ru, since both move the annual volume.
alpha.title: Alpha

kc.description: Crop coefficient applied to the loaded ETP: the soil evaporates at most kc x ETP a day. 1.0 takes the ETP as loaded, which assumes the surface of that ETP looks like the site: check what the product refers to. Between 0 and 2. Kept fixed by default: kc and ru move the same annual volume.
kc.title: Kc

impervious_fraction.description: Share of the area that is sealed (roofs, roads). The rain that falls on it runs off at once, with no infiltration and no evaporation, and reaches the streams, the lakes and the gauged discharge. The soil reservoir covers the rest of the area. From 0 up to, not including, 1. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.impervious_fraction]; the range belongs to the site, so a file has to state it.
impervious_fraction.title: Impervious Fraction

bypass_fraction.description: Share of the rain on the unsealed area that skips the soil through macropores and joins the recharge the same day, even when the soil is dry. From 0 up to, not including, 1. Keep it at 0 while K and Sy are calibrated: a bypass can rebuild the summer recharge the soil reservoir removes.
bypass_fraction.title: Bypass Fraction

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

transit_time.description: Mean time the water leaving the soil takes to cross the unsaturated zone down to the water table, in days. A linear reservoir with this time constant delays and smooths the recharge; 0 sends it the same day. A bare number is in days; "5 days" also reads. At most 30 days: a longer delay would rebuild the slow groundwater memory MODFLOW computes itself.
transit_time.title: Transit Time

curve_number.description: SCS curve number (AMC II), dimensionless, of a HELP-style surface runoff (Schroeder et al. 1994): the unsealed share of the rain above a daily retention loses some to a fast runoff, more as the soil is wetter. None turns the term off, bit for bit as before. Between 30 and 98. It reads the soil and never the water table, so it renders saturation runoff badly: leave it off where the drains already give that runoff. To calibrate it, state a range under [calibration.parameters.curve_number]: it belongs to the soil group and the land use of the site.
curve_number.title: Curve Number

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

runoff_time.description: Time constant of the linear reservoir that routes the curve-number runoff to the outlet, in days. No effect while curve_number is None. 0 sends it the same day; "2 days" also reads. Between 0 and 10 days: a longer delay would smooth away the fast surface peak the term exists for.
runoff_time.title: Runoff Time

anyOf.description: A quantity as text: a number then a unit, for example '150 m' or '0.36 m/h'.

runoff_lag.description: Pure delay applied to the routed curve-number runoff, after runoff_time, before it reaches the gauged discharge: the travel time to the outlet plus any lag between the forcing's daily step and the gauge's. No effect while curve_number is None. 0 adds no delay, bit for bit as before; "0.75 days" also reads, interpolated linearly between the neighbouring whole-day shifts. Between 0 and 5 days: a longer shift belongs to runoff_time's reservoir, not to a fixed travel time. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.runoff_lag].
runoff_lag.title: Runoff Lag

spinup.description: State of the soil on the first day. "first_year" repeats the first 365 days of the run until the storage at the end of that year moves by less than 0.1 mm, 20 times at most; the run must last 364 days (52 weeks) at least, and a 364-day run repeats those 364 days. "none" starts from a full soil, the state of a soil in a wet winter.
spinup.title: Spinup

value_docs.first_year: Repeat the first year until the soil storage settles.
value_docs.none: Start from a full soil and an empty transit store.

SolverConfig.description:
Configuration block defining the active groundwater solver engine.

The TOML form is ``backend = { kind = "modflow6" }`` for a built-in
backend, or ``backend = { kind = "custom", name = "x" }`` for a
plugin-registered backend.

It also carries the backend-agnostic preprocessing switches both MODFLOW
backends read, so one TOML key drives both. ``sink_fill`` and
``drain_band_depth_m`` both act on the drains of a depressed model top and
are mutually exclusive.

sink_fill.description: Dimensionless. Remove the drain from every cell sitting in a closed depression of the model top, by setting its DRN conductance to zero. A closed depression has no outlet, so water reaching it ponds instead of seeping into a stream, and a drain there invents a discharge point. The depressions are measured on the solver mesh, by a priority flood seeded on every cell water can leave the domain through; both MODFLOW backends read the same mask. This does NOT move the topography: no elevation is raised, no DEM is rewritten, and every other package sees the surface it would have seen. Refused when the mask cannot be built. The depressions are counted on the four shared faces MODFLOW connects, not on the eight neighbours a raster fill uses: the share of the mesh flagged is about twice as large on four faces as on eight neighbours, a factor that is the neighbourhood and nothing else. NOT SANCTIONED BY ANY SOURCE: no manual, no USGS document and no guideline removes a discharge boundary where a pit is detected, and measured here it degrades both scores. The remedy the USGS does document for the same question is solver.drain_band_depth_m, which gives every cell a discharge band instead of taking the drain away. Default false, which drains every cell as before.
sink_fill.title: Sink Fill

drain_bed_thickness_m.description: Metres. Thickness of the drain BED in the fallback conductance C = K * cell_area / bed_thickness, used when no drainage conductance is declared. A drain bed is the clogging layer at the bottom of a watercourse, decimetres to a metre; it is NOT the aquifer, and the layer thickness this used to borrow (tens of metres) has no physical relation to it. The value matters because it sets how much head the drain itself imposes to pass the recharge: dh = R * bed_thickness / K, independent of the cell size. For R = 439 mm/yr, 30 m gives 4.17 m of head at K = 1e-7 m/s and makes the drain the limiting resistance over two decades of a [1e-7, 1e-3] search; 1 m gives 13.9 cm and 0.1 m gives 1.4 cm. In this method the drain is a seepage face, so it must never limit: K and the recharge decide where water surfaces, not the boundary condition. Proportionality to K is preserved either way, so the K/R invariance the network criterion rests on is untouched. The value 1.0 is a convention with no measured source: no measurement and no document gives it, and it is kept as it is so that no earlier result moves. It stays in [solver], whatever the layer of the other drain keys. Write your own value when you have a measure.
drain_bed_thickness_m.title: Drain Bed Thickness M

drain_conductance_floor_m2_s.description: m2/s. Floor applied to every DRN conductance, whether declared or derived from hk. It exists for degenerate cells only, a zero-thickness or zero-conductivity cell whose formula would divide by zero or emit a zero-conductance drain MODFLOW reads as absent. It is not a physical choice and moving it does not tune anything: a real conductance on a real cell is many orders of magnitude above it. Raise it only to make a degenerate mesh audible.
drain_conductance_floor_m2_s.title: Drain Conductance Floor M2 S

drain_band_depth_m.description: Metres. Depth D of the sub-cell discharge band every drain cell gets instead of a single elevation: the drain sits at top - D/2 and its conductance is multiplied by top_layer_thickness / D. The multiplier is the thickness and not the cell area because the conductance it scales is already Kv*A/b, so scaling by b/D gives Kv*A/D, which is CDRN exactly; scaling by A/D would give an m3/s where a conductance is m2/s, too high by A/b. The cell therefore starts discharging before the head reaches its mean elevation, and discharges harder the higher the head climbs into the band. This answers the one question the USGS documents about a model top, that the land inside a cell is not flat: UZF1 exposes the same depth as SURFDEP, 'the average undulation depth within a finite-difference cell', and MODFLOW 6 carries it into DRN as DDRN, with HDRN = land surface - DDRN/2 and CDRN = Kv*A/DDRN. MODFLOW 6 solves its DDRN band with a smooth (linear then cubic) curve; the option here is the piecewise equivalent of the same idea, applied identically by both MODFLOW backends, so a later switch to the native smooth form is a documented refinement and not a surprise. It does NOT move the topography: no elevation is raised, no DEM is rewritten, and every other package sees the surface it would have seen. The seepage criterion is the one reader that cannot: a banded cell discharges at top - D/2 and never climbs back to top, so the mask follows the band and the run persists D in its store for every figure drawn afterwards. It classifies no cell: every drain cell gets the same band, so nothing has to be sorted into artefact and real. Pick D the way Feinstein et al. 2020 (Groundwater 58:524-534, doi:10.1111/gwat.12931) do, from the standard deviation of the fine land-surface elevations inside a cell; they obtain 0.61 m. Mutually exclusive with solver.sink_fill, which answers the same question by removing drains instead. Default 0.0: one elevation per drain, unchanged from every earlier run.
drain_band_depth_m.title: Drain Band Depth M

TopSamplingConfig.description:
How the top of the solver grid is sampled from the DEM.

Applies to the MODFLOW 6 runtime mesh and to a structured grid coarser than
its DEM (``[mesh] cell_size`` or ``[mesh.regular] shape``). The default 'centroid' mode
samples the DEM at each Voronoi generator, or resamples it to the grid, which
under-represents narrow incised channels (the sample lands on a bank, not the
thalweg). The 'zonal' mode reduces every DEM pixel inside a cell with a
per-class statistic (a thalweg-preserving stat on channel pixels, an area stat
on hillslope pixels), so channel cells keep their incised low. A structured
grid whose cells are the DEM pixels already holds the pixel
values and is unchanged. Only the top is zonal; the bottom keeps its rule. On
a structured grid the idomain does not move, and zonal applies only when a cell
covers at least two DEM pixels. MODFLOW-NWT builds no channel mask, so a zonal
top there needs ``channel_source = "none"`` (median only), and the config load
refuses the other value. Boussinesq ignores it. Every
non-default value changes the calibration params_hash (config-scoped); when
the sampling CODE changes, bump the version so the code-blind cache re-solves.

mode.description: Top-sampling strategy. 'centroid' samples the DEM at each cell generator, or resamples it to a structured grid (fast, the default). On a mesh that publishes a lateral offset for a river cell (the river runs through the cell but beside its centre, as where a contact line crosses it or two thalwegs share it), that cell takes the lowest DEM pixel it covers. 'zonal' reduces every DEM pixel inside a cell with per-class stats.
mode.title: Mode

hillslope_stat.description: Zonal statistic over non-channel (hillslope) pixels inside a cell.
hillslope_stat.title: Hillslope Stat

value_docs.max: Uses the highest hillslope pixel elevation found inside the cell.
value_docs.mean: Averages every hillslope pixel in the cell to set its top elevation.
value_docs.median: Uses the median hillslope pixel elevation, robust to outlier pixels.
value_docs.min: Uses the lowest hillslope pixel elevation found inside the cell.
value_docs.p10: Uses the 10th percentile of hillslope pixel elevations inside the cell.
value_docs.p25: Uses the 25th percentile of hillslope pixel elevations inside the cell.

channel_stat.description: Zonal statistic over channel pixels inside a cell (thalweg-preserving; 'min' keeps the incised low).
channel_stat.title: Channel Stat

value_docs.mean: Averages channel pixel elevations, smoothing over the incised thalweg.
value_docs.median: Uses the median channel pixel elevation, less aggressive than the thalweg low.
value_docs.min: Uses the lowest channel pixel elevation, keeping the incised thalweg low.
value_docs.p10: Uses the 10th percentile of channel pixel elevations, near the thalweg low.
value_docs.p25: Uses the 25th percentile of channel pixel elevations, above the thalweg low.

channel_source.description: Where channel pixels come from when mode='zonal'. 'streams_raster' uses the delineated river-network raster reprojected onto the DEM grid; 'none' disables the channel class (every pixel is hillslope).
channel_source.title: Channel Source

channel_buffer_px.description: Dilate the channel pixel mask by this many pixels before reducing, to capture a channel that grazes a cell without a pixel centre on it.
channel_buffer_px.title: Channel Buffer Px

spike_guard_tol_m.description: Revert a hillslope cell's zonal value to the centroid sample when it deviates more than this many metres (guards nodata/edge spikes); channel cells are exempt since they are lowered on purpose. 0 disables the guard.
spike_guard_tol_m.title: Spike Guard Tol M

min_pixels.description: Minimum DEM pixels inside a cell to trust a hillslope zonal statistic; below this the cell falls back to the centroid sample. A channel cell uses its channel stat from a single thalweg pixel.
min_pixels.title: Min Pixels

min_thickness_m.description: Minimum column thickness (m) kept under a zonal top lowered by a channel or a crossing. On a mesh of polygons the bottom of a cell whose lowered top leaves less than this, or less than a tenth of the column its centre sample gave, moves down with it and keeps the thickness of the cell-centre sample; on a regular grid the top is raised back instead.
min_thickness_m.title: Min Thickness M

VerticalGridConfig.description:
How the aquifer between the top and the base of ``[domain.depth_model]`` is split into layers.

It is the ``[domain.layers]`` table, read by every solver, so a project has one
layering whatever solver runs it. It holds the layering strategy
(``genmtd_lay``), the layer count, proportions or layer tables, the pinch-out
rule and the nodata sentinel.

All geometric quantities are interpreted in SI meters.

genmtd_lay.description: How the aquifer thickness is split into layers: equal layers, layers that thicken with depth, the fractions you list, or one base per layer.
genmtd_lay.title: Genmtd Lay

value_docs.constant: Splits local thickness into nlay equal-fraction layers at every cell.
value_docs.decay: Grows layer thickness geometrically with depth when lay_decay is above one.
value_docs.list: Uses the explicit per-layer thickness fractions given in lay_proportions.
value_docs.surfaces: Gives each layer its own base in the [[domain.layers.layer]] tables.

nlay.description: Number of layers for 'constant' and 'decay'. With 'list', the number of fractions sets it, with 'surfaces' the number of layer tables.
nlay.title: Nlay

lay_decay.description: Ratio of each layer's thickness to the thickness of the layer above it, above 1. With 2, each layer is twice as thick as the one above.
lay_decay.title: Lay Decay

lay_proportions.description: Share of the thickness each layer takes, from the top. The shares must sum to 1.
lay_proportions.title: Lay Proportions

layer.description: The layers from the top, each with its base, for 'surfaces'. The last layer ends on the base of [domain.depth_model] and gives no base.
layer.title: Layer

pinch_out.description: What a layer thinner than its min_thickness becomes, for 'surfaces'. Read only with that value of genmtd_lay.
pinch_out.title: Pinch Out

value_docs.keep_min_thickness: The base of the layer moves down to keep min_thickness, and the layers below and the base of the aquifer with it. MODFLOW-NWT reads only this value.
value_docs.pass_through: The cell becomes a vertical pass-through (idomain -1, MODFLOW 6 only) and the active cell below it, or above it at the base, takes its thickness.

WorkspaceConfig.description:
Strict-binary workspace configuration.

The canonical workspace layout is::

    <workspace>/
        workspace.toml
        data/
            cache.duckdb
        projects/
            <name>/
                project.toml   <- TOML lives here when using scaffold
                runs/<run>/
                .hmp/index.duckdb

Fields under ``[workspace]``:

``project_root`` (runtime only)
    Directory of the project. Set by the loader from the location of the
    file; refused when a file writes it.

``root`` (explicit workspace override)
    When set, the shared data workspace root. Derives ``data_dir``
    unless it is explicitly overridden.

``data_dir``
    Explicit override of the folder the input data are read from. The index
    (``catalog_path``) and the runs (``runs_dir``) are read-only properties,
    fixed by the storage layout contract.

Every output of a run lives in ``runs/<run>/``. The solver scratch of a
run is ``HMP_SCRATCH_ROOT``, else the default of the launcher.

description:
Top-level configuration for HydroModPy.

Aggregates sub-components (workspace, geographic, domain, data, flow,
transport, solver, modflownwt, modflow6, display)
into a centralized,
hierarchical model and validates optional flow parameters as
`FieldParamConfig` dictionaries.

workflow.description: Workflow configuration: `workflow.mode` ('simulation', 'calibration' or 'overview'), the console verbosity and the profiler. The mode is optional; unset, the sections of the file say what `hmp run` does.

workspace.description: Where the shared input data of the project are read and cached. The project root is the folder that holds project.toml, never a key of the file.

site.description: The catchment this project models: its name, label, gauge and registry URI. Required when geographic.catchment.kind declares a real catchment (from_outlet_coord, from_polyg_shp or dem); a synthetic domain has none. Refused beside [sites], where each case takes its site from a row of the site table.

sites.description: The catchments of a campaign and the recipes run on each of them: the plan is sites x recipes, one case <site>-<recipe> per pair. Refused beside [site].

metrics.description: Where and when a run is scored after it ends: the station (default [site] gauge) and the window. Without a window the scores are left empty.

publication.description: Licence, creators and attribution written into every copy hmp publish makes of a result. hmp publish --public refuses a project without a licence.

geographic.description: Configuration block for geographic and watershed delineation parameters.

domain.description: Domain configuration: the depth of the aquifer ([domain.depth_model]), its layering ([domain.layers], read by every solver) and the spatial-support mode used for heterogeneous parameter mapping (`none`, `geology`, or `zones`).

data.description: Data-managers configuration. Use `data.types` to declare requested families (for example `geology`). The launcher can also infer extra families from other sections (domain, flow), controlled by `data.inference_mode` ('warn' or 'strict').

flow.description: Flow process configuration with declared parameter ids in [flow].param_list and payloads validated from [flow.param.<id>] TOML sections.

transport.description: Transport process configuration, with solver-specific parameter blocks under [transport.modpath.parameters], [transport.mt3dms.parameters], and [transport.modflow6gwt.parameters].

simulation.description: Optional simulation orchestration block loaded from [simulation] and [[simulation.process]]. When absent, the launcher uses its default fixed phase order.

solver.description: Global solver block loaded from [solver]: the backend selector in [solver.backend], plus the backend-agnostic preprocessing switches both MODFLOW backends read (solver.sink_fill, solver.drain_band_depth_m).

modflownwt.description: MODFLOW-NWT settings: the top sampling of the grid ([modflownwt.sgrid.top_sampling]), the package options ([modflownwt.process_specific]) and the solver settings ([modflownwt.runtime.<package>], expert keys).

modflow6.description: MODFLOW 6 settings: the top sampling of the grid ([modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling]), the package options ([modflow6.process_specific]) and the solver settings ([modflow6.runtime], expert keys).

display.description: The figures a run draws, loaded from the [display] section.

export.description: The exports written at the end of a run, one [[export]] block per request, in the order of the file. Each block says what (variables), when (time or period) and where (folder or file); the format follows the data.
export.title: Export

observation.description: Observation points declared in [observation] and sampled while the run still holds its fields. Each [[observation.points]] entry names a location (x, y, and layer or depth); its series land in the run timeseries table, so no post-hoc interrogation is needed for a point known in advance.

overview.description: Optional overview report settings loaded from the [overview] section.  When present without [simulation], triggers the data-overview (watershed identity card) workflow.

mesh.description: Optional mesh settings loaded from the [mesh] section: which engine meshes the model ('regular', 'triangle' or 'voronoi') and how fine. Without the section the 'regular' engine meshes the model with the DEM pixels. The solver must read the cells of the engine, which is checked before any meshing.

calibration.description: Optional calibration settings loaded from the [calibration] section.  When present, triggers the calibration workflow. The section and the shape of CalibrationReport are experimental until the rework of the calibration is published.

spinup.description: Optional cyclic spin-up settings loaded from the [spinup] section. Drives 'hmp spinup': repeat a forcing window, restart each cycle from the previous state, until the heads and the lake stage converge.

base_config.description: Path of a TOML file this file extends, relative to this file. The keys written here replace the ones the base file sets. Lists replace the base list: the suffix __append extends it, __merge merges each table with the inherited one of the same id, name or source, and a key is removed with <key>__delete = true.

title: HydroModPyConfig
